chapters.title: Chapter 280: Alia Has Finally Found Her Perfect Partner!
paragraphs: The thought surfaced before he could suppress it.
And once it appeared, his mind began running wild.
After all, this wasn’t something unheard of within the Beast Empire.
There had been many cases where siblings had devoured one another’s power simply to strengthen themselves.
Even the Kings and Emperors didn’t interfere.
That was because the Beast Empire also followed this principle—
The strongest survived.
As long as someone possessed the strength to take another’s power, they had the right to do so.
Of course, such things couldn’t be done openly.
If discovered, the offender would be banished from the Beast Empire.
Soon.
Ivar’s eyes gradually filled with lust.
His imagination began painting an image of Alia naked body lying in his bed.
The thought made his sinister smile deepen.
"Ivar, are you okay?"
Nolan’s voice suddenly came from his left.
The unexpected question snapped Ivar out of his increasingly frantic thoughts.
His expression froze for a brief moment.
Then he took a slow, deep breath.
He forcibly pushed those urges back down, restoring his usual calm expression before turning toward Nolan.
"I am fine."
His voice sounded completely normal.
But Nolan wasn’t convinced. Something felt wrong.
Kira seemed to sense it as well.
The two exchanged a brief glance but chose not to question him.
Instead, they simply nodded.
"We’ll leave first."
Both of them rose from their seats and left the room, intending to prepare a few more things before the upcoming exploration.
Ivar watched them leave without saying anything.
His expression remained calm.
But beneath that calm exterior—
His earlier thoughts still lingered.
A few moments later, Ivar also rose from his seat and decided to leave.
The Elves and the Marinthians had already departed.
Still, before walking away, he turned his head one final time.
His gaze settled on Alia.
Then, without saying a word, he turned around and left the room completely.
The moment Ivar crossed the gate and disappeared from sight, the smile Alia had maintained the entire time vanished.
Her expression instantly became serious.
Luke, however, didn’t notice the change.
He was still focused on calming down Selene, who hadn’t completely gotten over what had happened earlier.
’I have to hurry.’ Alia’s thoughts were filled with worry.
She knew very well what Ivar had been doing.
He had already taken the same type of ability from several women and incorporated them into his own power, using them to continuously strengthen himself.
Yet Alia had never done anything like that.
Not even once.
Since, she didn’t want to sacrifice her chastity to some random person merely for the sake of increasing her strength.
That was precisely why she had been searching for someone suitable.
Someone strong enough to withstand her.
Someone talented enough to recover quickly.
If she found such a person, she could form a Dual Cultivation relationship with him and steadily increase her own strength.
And while he recovered, she could protect him.
That was the plan she had always intended to follow.
But now—
Alia’s gaze quietly shifted toward Luke.
The moment she saw him, a thought surfaced in her mind.
’He’s perfect.’
After all, heroes weren’t something that grew on trees.
And the Hero of their Beast Empire was someone who openly chose to take female cultivation and even their abilities.
That was precisely why Alia couldn’t afford to get anywhere near him.
She had to protect her chastity from too many people—her own royal family, the Emperor’s royal family, and even the Hero of their own empire.
After all, her first time would bring the maximum benefits from her partner.
Thinking about this, Alia let out a quiet sigh before also deciding to leave the room.
She still had a few things to prepare if she truly wanted to get close to Luke.
Luke noticed Alia leaving—
"What are you looking at?"
Before he could even finish turning his head, Selene suddenly cupped his face with both hands and forcefully turned it back toward her.
"Only look at me." Her crimson eyes stared directly into his blue ones.
Luke blinked.
Then, slowly nodded, silently pleading for her to let go of his face.
"Good boy." Seeing him obediently nod, Selene gave his head a small pat.
Pat, pat.
The gesture immediately drew strange looks from Zeyr and Karon, who were now the only other people remaining in the meeting room.
Luke noticed their gazes.
His mouth twitched.
’She’s treating me exactly like she did when we first met.’
Back then, he had merely been a mortal who had just arrived in this world and knew absolutely nothing about it.
And now, after everything that had happened, she was still treating him like that helpless newcomer.
Luke could only sigh inwardly.
"Let’s go."
Taking advantage of the moment, he grabbed Selene’s hand and quickly pulled her toward the exit.
He left the room with her before the situation could become any more embarrassing.
Zeyr and Karon watched the two leave.
For a moment, they remained silent.
Then they exchanged amused glances.
Without saying anything, they also stood up and followed after them.
Three hours later, everyone gathered inside a secret room within the royal palace.
This was the room that contained the pathway leading directly to the ruins.
"I hope all of you are ready," Roderan said as he looked around at everyone.
One by one, they nodded.
Twelve representatives from the Empyrean Academy had gathered.
Alongside them were twelve members from Horizon Academy, including Estelle and Isaria.
The Eldric Royal Palace had also prepared a hundred Early B-Rank beings.
Ten were mages.
The remaining ninety were Platinum Knights.
These weren’t ordinary guards, either.
They were the same people who had entered the ruins before—and, despite the dangers within, had managed to survive and return.
Counting everyone, there were currently 125 people gathered in the secret room, Luke included.
Roderan’s expression soon became somewhat helpless.
"Unfortunately, no one above the Early B-Rank realm can enter these ruins."
A sigh escaped his lips.
He had wanted to explore this ancient place himself more than anyone.
But as an A-Rank being, he couldn’t even step inside.
The restriction was absolute.
Hearing this, nobody else showed the slightest surprise.
They had already known about this limitation beforehand.
Only Luke raised his brows once again.
Then, without wasting any more time, Roderan waved his hand.
His movement was so fast that none of them could even see it properly.
They only knew that he had done something.
The next moment—
Crack!
The space in mid-air split apart, revealing another space on the other side.
Beyond it was a massive chamber.
And standing within that chamber was an ancient gate, towering thousands of feet.
Roderan barely spared it a glance.
Instead, he stepped forward and raised both hands.
In the next instant, they became covered in red essence.
But unlike the flowing essence Luke had seen from B-Rank beings, this essence didn’t flow around his palm.
It was solid.
It completely covered his hands like a pair of solid essence gauntlets.
Then Roderan tightened his grip.
Without using any special technique, he relied solely on the strength of his body and grabbed the edges of the spatial cut.
RIIIP!
He forcefully tore the narrow, single-line opening apart.
The spatial cut widened rapidly, transforming into a broad passage large enough for everyone to enter.
WHOOSH!
A few violent shockwaves erupted from the spatial passage.
Few B-Rank beings from Horizon academy were caught off guard and were pushed backward.
Fortunately, Selene immediately shielded Luke from the incoming force.
Otherwise, without activating his Titan form, Luke would have been sent crashing into the wall.
Once the shockwaves finally settled, Luke looked toward the passage ahead and then to Roderan.
’Damn, so cool.’
After all, normally, only Space users—or mages who possessed sufficient knowledge of Space magic—could open a spatial passage.
But that rule didn’t apply to A-Rank beings and those above them.
They could use their raw essence or raw physical power to directly tear apart space itself.
"This passage won’t remain open for long, so enter now."
Roderan’s voice immediately brought everyone’s attention back to the matter at hand.
The spatial passage was already beginning to tremble slightly as the surrounding space attempted to repair itself.
Everyone nodded.
The hundred B-Rank beings entered first.
After them, the members of Horizon Academy followed one after another.
Then came the representatives from the Empyrean Academy.
Finally, Luke and Selene stepped through the passage together.
Roderan and Drevian remained behind, watching their departing figures.
Neither of them looked relaxed.
There was clear worry in their eyes.
This time, too many important figures had entered the ruins.
If even one of them died inside—
The consequences would be catastrophic for their kingdom.
"I hope everyone will be alright." Roderan’s voice carried a trace of concern.
The very next moment, the spatial passage completely closed.
Crack.
The rift disappeared without a trace, completely concealing whatever secrets were hidden beyond it.

sentences.text: The thought surfaced before he could suppress it.
And once it appeared, his mind began running wild.
After all, this wasn’t something unheard of within the Beast Empire.
There had been many cases where siblings had devoured one another’s power simply to strengthen themselves.
Even the Kings and Emperors didn’t interfere.
That was because the Beast Empire also followed this principle—
The strongest survived.
As long as someone possessed the strength to take another’s power, they had the right to do so.
Of course, such things couldn’t be done openly.
If discovered, the offender would be banished from the Beast Empire.
Soon.
Ivar’s eyes gradually filled with lust.
His imagination began painting an image of Alia naked body lying in his bed.
The thought made his sinister smile deepen.
"Ivar, are you okay?"
Nolan’s voice suddenly came from his left.
The unexpected question snapped Ivar out of his increasingly frantic thoughts.
His expression froze for a brief moment.
Then he took a slow, deep breath.
He forcibly pushed those urges back down, restoring his usual calm expression before turning toward Nolan.
"I am fine."
His voice sounded completely normal.
But Nolan wasn’t convinced.
Something felt wrong.
Kira seemed to sense it as well.
The two exchanged a brief glance but chose not to question him.
Instead, they simply nodded.
"We’ll leave first."
Both of them rose from their seats and left the room, intending to prepare a few more things before the upcoming exploration.
Ivar watched them leave without saying anything.
His expression remained calm.
But beneath that calm exterior—
His earlier thoughts still lingered.
A few moments later, Ivar also rose from his seat and decided to leave.
The Elves and the Marinthians had already departed.
Still, before walking away, he turned his head one final time.
His gaze settled on Alia.
Then, without saying a word, he turned around and left the room completely.
The moment Ivar crossed the gate and disappeared from sight, the smile Alia had maintained the entire time vanished.
Her expression instantly became serious.
Luke, however, didn’t notice the change.
He was still focused on calming down Selene, who hadn’t completely gotten over what had happened earlier.
’I have to hurry.’ Alia’s thoughts were filled with worry.
She knew very well what Ivar had been doing.
He had already taken the same type of ability from several women and incorporated them into his own power, using them to continuously strengthen himself.
Yet Alia had never done anything like that.
Not even once.
Since, she didn’t want to sacrifice her chastity to some random person merely for the sake of increasing her strength.
That was precisely why she had been searching for someone suitable.
Someone strong enough to withstand her.
Someone talented enough to recover quickly.
If she found such a person, she could form a Dual Cultivation relationship with him and steadily increase her own strength.
And while he recovered, she could protect him.
That was the plan she had always intended to follow.
But now—
Alia’s gaze quietly shifted toward Luke.
The moment she saw him, a thought surfaced in her mind.
’He’s perfect.’
After all, heroes weren’t something that grew on trees.
And the Hero of their Beast Empire was someone who openly chose to take female cultivation and even their abilities.
That was precisely why Alia couldn’t afford to get anywhere near him.
She had to protect her chastity from too many people—her own royal family, the Emperor’s royal family, and even the Hero of their own empire.
After all, her first time would bring the maximum benefits from her partner.
Thinking about this, Alia let out a quiet sigh before also deciding to leave the room.
She still had a few things to prepare if she truly wanted to get close to Luke.
Luke noticed Alia leaving—
"What are you looking at?"
Before he could even finish turning his head, Selene suddenly cupped his face with both hands and forcefully turned it back toward her.
"Only look at me." Her crimson eyes stared directly into his blue ones.
Luke blinked.
Then, slowly nodded, silently pleading for her to let go of his face.
"Good boy." Seeing him obediently nod, Selene gave his head a small pat.
Pat, pat.
The gesture immediately drew strange looks from Zeyr and Karon, who were now the only other people remaining in the meeting room.
Luke noticed their gazes.
His mouth twitched.
’She’s treating me exactly like she did when we first met.’
Back then, he had merely been a mortal who had just arrived in this world and knew absolutely nothing about it.
And now, after everything that had happened, she was still treating him like that helpless newcomer.
Luke could only sigh inwardly.
"Let’s go."
Taking advantage of the moment, he grabbed Selene’s hand and quickly pulled her toward the exit.
He left the room with her before the situation could become any more embarrassing.
Zeyr and Karon watched the two leave.
For a moment, they remained silent.
Then they exchanged amused glances.
Without saying anything, they also stood up and followed after them.
Three hours later, everyone gathered inside a secret room within the royal palace.
This was the room that contained the pathway leading directly to the ruins.
"I hope all of you are ready," Roderan said as he looked around at everyone.
One by one, they nodded.
Twelve representatives from the Empyrean Academy had gathered.
Alongside them were twelve members from Horizon Academy, including Estelle and Isaria.
The Eldric Royal Palace had also prepared a hundred Early B-Rank beings.
Ten were mages.
The remaining ninety were Platinum Knights.
These weren’t ordinary guards, either.
They were the same people who had entered the ruins before—and, despite the dangers within, had managed to survive and return.
Counting everyone, there were currently 125 people gathered in the secret room, Luke included.
Roderan’s expression soon became somewhat helpless.
"Unfortunately, no one above the Early B-Rank realm can enter these ruins."
A sigh escaped his lips.
He had wanted to explore this ancient place himself more than anyone.
But as an A-Rank being, he couldn’t even step inside.
The restriction was absolute.
Hearing this, nobody else showed the slightest surprise.
They had already known about this limitation beforehand.
Only Luke raised his brows once again.
Then, without wasting any more time, Roderan waved his hand.
His movement was so fast that none of them could even see it properly.
They only knew that he had done something.
The next moment—
Crack!
The space in mid-air split apart, revealing another space on the other side.
Beyond it was a massive chamber.
And standing within that chamber was an ancient gate, towering thousands of feet.
Roderan barely spared it a glance.
Instead, he stepped forward and raised both hands.
In the next instant, they became covered in red essence.
But unlike the flowing essence Luke had seen from B-Rank beings, this essence didn’t flow around his palm.
It was solid.
It completely covered his hands like a pair of solid essence gauntlets.
Then Roderan tightened his grip.
Without using any special technique, he relied solely on the strength of his body and grabbed the edges of the spatial cut.
RIIIP!
He forcefully tore the narrow, single-line opening apart.
The spatial cut widened rapidly, transforming into a broad passage large enough for everyone to enter.
WHOOSH!
A few violent shockwaves erupted from the spatial passage.
Few B-Rank beings from Horizon academy were caught off guard and were pushed backward.
Fortunately, Selene immediately shielded Luke from the incoming force.
Otherwise, without activating his Titan form, Luke would have been sent crashing into the wall.
Once the shockwaves finally settled, Luke looked toward the passage ahead and then to Roderan.
’Damn, so cool.’
After all, normally, only Space users—or mages who possessed sufficient knowledge of Space magic—could open a spatial passage.
But that rule didn’t apply to A-Rank beings and those above them.
They could use their raw essence or raw physical power to directly tear apart space itself.
"This passage won’t remain open for long, so enter now."
Roderan’s voice immediately brought everyone’s attention back to the matter at hand.
The spatial passage was already beginning to tremble slightly as the surrounding space attempted to repair itself.
Everyone nodded.
The hundred B-Rank beings entered first.
After them, the members of Horizon Academy followed one after another.
Then came the representatives from the Empyrean Academy.
Finally, Luke and Selene stepped through the passage together.
Roderan and Drevian remained behind, watching their departing figures.
Neither of them looked relaxed.
There was clear worry in their eyes.
This time, too many important figures had entered the ruins.
If even one of them died inside—
The consequences would be catastrophic for their kingdom.
"I hope everyone will be alright." Roderan’s voice carried a trace of concern.
The very next moment, the spatial passage completely closed.
Crack.
The rift disappeared without a trace, completely concealing whatever secrets were hidden beyond it.

chapters.title: Chapter 281: The Gods Were Worshipping Someone?!
paragraphs: The same day, the same year.
After stepping through the passage, everyone found themselves inside a vast underground chamber.
The room was ancient, and its walls were covered in carvings depicting battles between gods.
But there was something strange about them.
The enemies of those gods were nowhere to be seen.
The carvings clearly showed the gods attacking something, yet the figures on the opposite side had been completely erased.
It was almost as though they had been fighting against invisible enemies.
Luke’s gaze soon moved toward the front of the chamber.
There stood the enormous ancient gate, towering thousands of meters high.
It, too, was covered in carvings.
But unlike the battle scenes around them, the carvings on the gate depicted something entirely different.
They were showing worship.
’Worshipping?’ Luke’s eyes became strange as he stared at the images.
The carvings seemed to depict gods bowing before and worshipping someone.
’A god... worshipping another?’
Just thinking about it was enough to make Luke’s worldview tremble.
Gods were supposed to be those high and mighty beings standing above countless existences.
Yet someone had actually made them lower their heads.
’Just how much strength would someone need to make gods worship them?’ Luke couldn’t even begin to imagine it.
However, he quickly shook his head, forcing those thoughts away.
There was no point in dwelling on something he couldn’t comprehend.
He then turned his attention away from the carvings and looked around at everyone present.
The hundred B-Rank warriors of the Sunborn Kingdom were already preparing themselves, checking their equipment and securing their weapons before the expedition began.
The representatives of the Empyrean Academy, however, were far more interested in the carvings.
Selene was among them, her gaze lingering on the ancient scenes etched into the walls.
But when their attention eventually shifted toward the enormous gate, the reaction was immediate.
Even they looked stunned.
’So they found it strange too.’ Luke couldn’t help but find their expressions amusing.
Yet another thought soon entered his mind.
’Do those gods even know these carvings exist?’ His lips curled slightly.
And if they do... what would their expressions be when their own believers discover that those supposedly untouchable gods once bowed before someone else?
The thought alone was enough to bring a mocking smile to Luke’s face.
For some reason, it reminded him of the myths from his original world.
’Gods who were supposed to be divine, yet were just as flawed and hypocritical as mortals.’
Maybe too much evidence was left behind.
Perhaps there had simply been too many traces of what happened during twilight era.
And before those gods were expelled, they hadn’t been able to erase every single one.
The more Luke thought about it, the more convincing the possibility became.
Maybe that was one of the reasons the people of Valtharion—even the strongest among them—didn’t truly worship gods.
Outside of the churches, most simply regarded them as another form of existence.
An existence far stronger than themselves, certainly.
But still an existence.
They bowed when necessary, especially when seeking their help against demons.
But the mortals at the very bottom know none of this.
Luke’s eyes flickered.
For the first time since arriving in Valtharion, he felt that he had managed to uncover a small piece of the truth surrounding its gods.
However, before Luke could think any further, Estelle suddenly addressed everyone.
"Everyone." Her voice carried across the chamber.
One by one, the conversations stopped, and every gaze turned toward her.
Estelle waited until she had everyone’s attention before continuing in a serious tone.
"Once we enter the ruins, every person will be teleported to a random location."
She paused.
"Alone."
The single word immediately changed the atmosphere.
The expressions of the Empyrean Academy representatives shifted, and even Luke’s face changed.
’They hadn’t been told about this.’
Estelle clearly noticed their reactions, but she didn’t show the slightest hesitation.
After all, anyone entering these ruins had to understand the risks involved.
The dangers were severe enough that even the Empyrean Academy would have reconsidered sending people here if they had known every detail beforehand.
That was precisely why this information had been left out.
Estelle continued, her expression becoming even more solemn.
"The interior is a massive maze, filled with monsters that have been sleeping for thousands of years."
Her gaze swept across everyone.
"And that’s not all. There are constructs, traps, formations, and other dangers scattered throughout the ruins."
She paused briefly.
"Every one of them can be deadly."
"And, We’ve already lost many people inside."
The room became noticeably quieter.
"So once you’re inside, remain extremely cautious. And above all else, try to locate the nearest person as quickly as possible."
With that, Estelle finally finished explaining.
She sincerely hoped they would be able to find one another soon.
Unfortunately, there was one problem.
They barely understood the ruins themselves.
They didn’t know where the pathways would lead, where the monsters slept, or where the various traps and formations had been placed.
So after entering—
There was little they could rely on.
Except luck.
Still, Estelle added one final piece of information.
"Fortunately, you only need to survive for thirteen days inside."
She paused before continuing.
"After that, a portal leading back outside will appear."
The announcement didn’t cause much of a reaction.
Everyone already knew about the thirteen-day limit.
Yet the tension in the room remained. The earlier revelation that they would be separated immediately upon entering had clearly unsettled them.
Estelle sighed inwardly as she noticed their expressions.
Even she couldn’t do anything about it.
There was one more thing she hadn’t told them.
Something far more important.
Something that, if handled carelessly, could cost them their lives.
’I just hope none of them provokes a being above the Early B-Rank.’
Estelle’s gaze swept across the gathered people, worry evident in her eyes.
From the outside, the ruins could only be entered by those at Early B-Rank or below.
But that restriction didn’t necessarily apply to what already existed inside.
Estelle herself didn’t understand why.
Perhaps some mechanism within the ruins had malfunctioned after surviving for so many years.
Perhaps there was another reason entirely.
They simply didn’t know.
What they had discovered, however, was reassuring to a certain extent.
No being above the B-Rank realm had ever been found inside.
It was almost as if the ruins themselves rejected their existence.
Still, that didn’t mean the danger was insignificant.
Estelle’s gaze eventually settled on Isaria.
Worry again, surfaced in her eyes.
Isaria was only at the Early Golden Knight level.
Her cultivation was considerably lower than most of the people they were bringing into the ruins.
Yet they had still decided to bring her.
Because her Origin Skill could prove tremendously valuable during the exploration.
And that alone was worth taking the risk.
’Just stay safe, Isaria.’

chapters.title: Chapter 282: The Three-Way Chain No One Knows About!
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Luke’s expression was no better.
His gaze remained fixed on Selene, and the worry in his eyes was impossible to hide.
Selene was looking at him the same way.
She stepped closer until there was barely any distance between them, then gently raised her hand and caressed his face.
"Make sure you keep yourself safe." Her voice was soft, carrying a concern.
She leaned forward and pressed a gentle kiss against him.
Then, after pulling back just enough to look into his eyes, she whispered,
"I will find you, okay?"
It wasn’t merely a promise. She was asking him to promise her the same.
Luke continued staring at her with those worried eyes for a moment before answering.
"You keep yourself safe, and I will find you."
As soon as those words left his mouth, he pulled her into a tight embrace.
Selene was caught slightly off guard by his sudden action.
But after a brief moment, she relaxed and wrapped her arms around him as well, silently remaining in his embrace.
A short distance away, Alia watched the entire scene.
Unlike the others, however, there wasn’t even a trace of worry on her face.
Instead—
A bright smile slowly bloomed across her lips.
’Now Luke will be all mine.’ She thought about it excitedly.
For everyone else, being separated was a problem.
For her?
It wasn’t.
The Half-Owl race possessed an innate ability that allowed them to place a mark on another person and locate that individual regardless of the distance between them.
There were, of course, limitations.
The mark could be removed if someone powerful enough interfered with it or cleansed it.
But it wasn’t a death mark, a hostile mark, or even a conventional tracking mark.
Because of that, the person carrying the mark couldn’t even detect its existence.
And Alia had already placed hers on Luke.
She had done so earlier—
When she touched his waist.
Meanwhile, on the other side, Isaria quietly watched Luke and Selene embracing.
For some reason, the sight didn’t make her feel disappointed.
Instead, a strange thought surfaced in her mind.
’Even fate is helping me.’ Her eyes lingered on Luke.
’Luke and I... alone inside the ruins.’
That thought alone made her heart beat a little faster.
Earlier, she had nearly forced herself to abandon such thoughts.
She already knew how deeply Luke loved her.
But that only made things more difficult.
He already had a wife.
How could she bring herself to confess her feelings and come between them?
Yet the misunderstanding from their first encounter had never truly disappeared either.
Luke’s earlier outburst of anticipation...
Isaria had already decided that it had been directed toward her.
Because of that, she had never truly believed his explanation at the canteen.
The claim that it had all been a misunderstanding.
Her Origin Skill was perfectly suited for pathfinding, making her extremely valuable for this expedition.
But there were secrets about that ability that she had never revealed.
Not to anyone.
Not even to Estelle, her best friend.
She could mark someone. And the person she marked wouldn’t even realize it.
But her mark was fundamentally different from an ordinary tracking ability.
It acted almost like a Life Bond Mark.
Once placed, Valtharion itself would allow her to find that person, no matter where he went.
Distance didn’t matter.
As long as the mark remained, she could find him.
If Alia ever learned about this ability, she would be shocked beyond words.
Because it was remarkably similar to an ancient rumor surrounding the Half-Owl clan.
A legend claimed that when a Half-Owl became a complete Owl, they would have the chance to awaken such an ability.
An ability that could not be forcefully canceled.
Because it wasn’t merely their own power supporting it.
Valtharion itself was assisting them.
’Soon.’ With that thought lingering in her mind, Isaria turned and walked toward Estelle, who was calling for her.
She had no idea that someone else had already chosen her as his target.
’Soon, you will be mine.’ A smile of anticipation appeared on Ivar’s face.
He had secretly placed his own mark on Isaria as well.
That way, even if they were separated inside the maze, he would still be able to find her.
And so—
One person had secretly marked another.
That person had secretly marked someone else.
Neither of them knew that they, too, had already been marked.
A strange chain had formed without any of them realizing it.
"Let’s move." Estelle finally gave the order.
Then, she turned toward the Sunborn warriors and gave a slight nod.
Immediately, fifty Early Platinum Knights stepped forward.

Their platinum-colored armor gleamed beneath the dim light of the ruins. On each warrior’s back was the unmistakable emblem of the Sunborn Kingdom, while at the center of their chest armor was a small circular crest, each one glowing with a different elemental color.
Red for fire.
Blue for water.
Green for earth.
White for wind.
Purple for lightning.
And many others.
The fifty warriors reached the colossal gate and placed both hands against its surface.
For a brief moment, everything fell silent.
Then—
"HAAAAAAH!" A thunderous roar erupted from the warriors.
All fifty pushed with every ounce of their strength.
Their muscles bulged beneath their armor. Veins stood out along their arms and necks as their feet dug into the stone floor.
CRACK!
The ground beneath several warriors’ feet fractured under the immense force.
Yet the gate remained completely unmoved.
Not even an inch.
"Push harder!"
"RAAAAAH!"
The warriors gritted their teeth and continued pushing.
Still, nothing happened.
Estelle’s eyes narrowed.
"Forty more."
At her command, another forty Platinum Knights rushed forward.
They joined the others, placing their hands against the enormous gate.
"Ngh!"
"AAAAAH!"
"Push!"
"KEEP PUSHING!"
A chorus of roars echoed throughout the ruins.
Ninty Platinum Knights now strained against the gate.
The stone beneath their feet continued cracking.
Yet the gate...
Still refused to move.
Then—
Grrrrrrrrrrr.
A deep, grinding sound suddenly echoed through the ruins.
The gate had moved.
"It’s opening!"
"Keep pushing!"
"Don’t stop!"
The warriors roared with renewed strength.
Their faces turned red from exertion as they pushed harder than before.
GRRRRRRRRRR—
The colossal gate slowly began sliding inward.
An groan reverberated through the ruins as dust cascaded from its surface.
Then—
BOOOOOOM!
The gate slammed against the wall at the end of the entrance.
Silence descended. Dust slowly drifted through the air.
Everyone stared ahead.
Luke’s eyes widened slightly. "...A hallway?"
Instead of the ancient ruins they had expected, a vast hallway stretched before them.
It was enormous. And at the very end a blue light shimmered.
’A portal.’

Because of that, she had never truly believed his explanation at the canteen.
The claim that it had all been a misunderstanding.
Her Origin Skill was perfectly suited for pathfinding, making her extremely valuable for this expedition.
But there were secrets about that ability that she had never revealed.
Not to anyone.
Not even to Estelle, her best friend.
She could mark someone.
And the person she marked wouldn’t even realize it.
But her mark was fundamentally different from an ordinary tracking ability.
It acted almost like a Life Bond Mark.
Once placed, Valtharion itself would allow her to find that person, no matter where he went.
Distance didn’t matter.
As long as the mark remained, she could find him.
If Alia ever learned about this ability, she would be shocked beyond words.
Because it was remarkably similar to an ancient rumor surrounding the Half-Owl clan.
A legend claimed that when a Half-Owl became a complete Owl, they would have the chance to awaken such an ability.
An ability that could not be forcefully canceled.
Because it wasn’t merely their own power supporting it.
Valtharion itself was assisting them.
’Soon.’ With that thought lingering in her mind, Isaria turned and walked toward Estelle, who was calling for her.
She had no idea that someone else had already chosen her as his target.
’Soon, you will be mine.’ A smile of anticipation appeared on Ivar’s face.
He had secretly placed his own mark on Isaria as well.
That way, even if they were separated inside the maze, he would still be able to find her.
And so—
One person had secretly marked another.
That person had secretly marked someone else.
Neither of them knew that they, too, had already been marked.
A strange chain had formed without any of them realizing it.
"Let’s move." Estelle finally gave the order.
Then, she turned toward the Sunborn warriors and gave a slight nod.
Immediately, fifty Early Platinum Knights stepped forward.
Their platinum-colored armor gleamed beneath the dim light of the ruins.
On each warrior’s back was the unmistakable emblem of the Sunborn Kingdom, while at the center of their chest armor was a small circular crest, each one glowing with a different elemental color.
Red for fire.
Blue for water.
Green for earth.
White for wind.
Purple for lightning.
And many others.
The fifty warriors reached the colossal gate and placed both hands against its surface.
For a brief moment, everything fell silent.
Then—
"HAAAAAAH!" A thunderous roar erupted from the warriors.
All fifty pushed with every ounce of their strength.
Their muscles bulged beneath their armor.
Veins stood out along their arms and necks as their feet dug into the stone floor.
CRACK!
The ground beneath several warriors’ feet fractured under the immense force.
Yet the gate remained completely unmoved.
Not even an inch.
"Push harder!"
"RAAAAAH!"
The warriors gritted their teeth and continued pushing.
Still, nothing happened.
Estelle’s eyes narrowed.
"Forty more."
At her command, another forty Platinum Knights rushed forward.
They joined the others, placing their hands against the enormous gate.
"Ngh!"
"AAAAAH!"
"Push!"
"KEEP PUSHING!"
A chorus of roars echoed throughout the ruins.
Ninty Platinum Knights now strained against the gate.
The stone beneath their feet continued cracking.
Yet the gate...
Still refused to move.
Then—
Grrrrrrrrrrr.
A deep, grinding sound suddenly echoed through the ruins.
The gate had moved.
"It’s opening!"
"Keep pushing!"
"Don’t stop!"
The warriors roared with renewed strength.
Their faces turned red from exertion as they pushed harder than before.
GRRRRRRRRRR—
The colossal gate slowly began sliding inward.
An groan reverberated through the ruins as dust cascaded from its surface.
Then—
BOOOOOOM!
The gate slammed against the wall at the end of the entrance.
Silence descended.
Dust slowly drifted through the air.
Everyone stared ahead.
Luke’s eyes widened slightly.
"...A hallway?"
Instead of the ancient ruins they had expected, a vast hallway stretched before them.
It was enormous.
And at the very end a blue light shimmered.
’A portal.’

chapters.title: Chapter 283: Paragon’s Judgment Unlocks a New Power! [GOLDEN TICKET AND POWER STONE BONUS - ]
paragraphs: Estelle stared at the distant blue light for several seconds before raising her hand.
"Everyone, move." Without hesitation, she stepped forward.
The Sunborn warriors followed behind her.
One by one, the representatives and their groups began entering the hallway.
Luke glanced toward Selene.
Estelle had already warned them.
That the moment someone entered the portal, they would be teleported to a random location somewhere inside the enormous maze.
Then—
One person after another disappeared into the portal.
Whoosh!
Another figure vanished.
Whoosh!
Another.
Soon, only Luke and Selene remained.
They looked at each other one last time.
Then, without letting go of each other’s hands—
They stepped into the blue light.
WHOOSH!
The hallway had become completely empty.
Or so it seemed.
The next moment—
A black teleportation magic circle silently appeared across the floor.
Fwoosh!
Red flames suddenly erupted from its surface, engulfing the entire circle.
Three figures emerged from within.
All three were dressed in black robes, their bodies completely concealed from head to toe.
Yet there was one detail that immediately stood out.
On the back of each robe was the same symbol—
A golden broken mask, surrounded by three black flames.
The moment the three figures stepped out, the black magic circle vanished.
Not even a trace remained, as though it had never existed.
The figure standing at the front slowly raised his head.
His gaze settled upon the glowing blue portal ahead.
Then, in a deep and solemn voice, he spoke.
"Beyond the cracks lies the truth!"
A voice immediately answered from behind him.
"Beyond the truth lies our salvation!"
Silence followed.
Without another word, all three figures stepped forward and entered the blue portal.
And once the last figure passed through—
The hallway became empty once more.
As though no one had ever been there.
Deep within one of the maze’s dark pathways, several strange beasts silently prowled through the darkness.
They stood nearly ten feet tall, their bodies covered in thick armor resembling that of crocodiles.
Yet their legs were anything but normal.
Four long, spider-like legs extended from their bodies, allowing them to effortlessly crawl along both the ground and the towering walls.
And perhaps the most disturbing part—
They had no eyes. Not even empty sockets.
They were completely blind.
Instead, their oversized ears twitched constantly, sensing every faint sound that traveled through the maze.
At first glance, anyone encountering them for the first time would probably describe them in the simplest way possible—
A blind crocodile with spider legs.
And now, pathways, they themselves were enormous.
Most stretched roughly one hundred meters across, although some were far wider, reaching up to a full kilometer.
Yet one hundred meters was the narrowest a pathway could become.
There was no open sky above them, either.
The ceiling was sealed by the same dark material that formed the walls, completely enclosing each passage.
To reach another pathway, one had no choice but to travel through the connected routes of the maze.
The beasts continued moving forward, their movements surprisingly quiet despite their huge bodies.
They were clearly hunting.
Other creatures inhabited this place, and those creatures were their food.
As for where these beasts had originally come from...
That was something only the curious would have to uncover.
Fortunately for them, however, they wouldn’t need to travel very far for their next meal.
Because in the middle of the dark pathway—
Fwoosh!
A small blue light suddenly appeared.
Its glow spread through the darkness, illuminating the surrounding walls.
The beasts immediately stopped. Their ears twitched.
And although they possessed no eyes—
The blue light seemed to have awakened something within them.
"Food delivery system has arrived."
It wasn’t the first time they had seen something like this.
Over the past few years, many unfortunate beings had appeared through those blue lights and ended up becoming food for the creatures dwelling inside the maze.
So when the light appeared again, the five beasts didn’t seem surprised.
All five were Peak Blood Awakening beasts, equivalent to Peak D-Rank beings.
They exchanged glances.
Then, almost as though they had already decided who would take the first bite, they slowly moved toward the glowing blue light.
Their spider-like legs tapped against the ground as they surrounded their incoming meal.
Soon, the blue light flickered.
Flicker... flicker...
And a figure suddenly appeared within it.
Sadly, the person hadn’t even had the chance to properly look around.
"GRAAAH!"
When, all five beasts pounced at once.
They opened their jaws and lunged forward, eager to devour their meal before the others could take it.
Of course, after finishing their food, they would surely express their gratitude toward the unfortunate soul for generously offering himself to them.
But—
"Not a very nice welcome, I guess."
The calm voice instantly interrupted their charge.
The next moment—
SHING!
A brilliant golden sword light flashed outward in a perfect circular motion.
For an instant, everything became still.
Then—
Thud.
One head rolled across the ground.
Thud! Thud! Thud! Thud!
The remaining four heads followed.
All five Peak D-Rank beasts had been decapitated in an instant.
Their large bodies collapsed a moment later.
BAM!
They hit the ground heavily, lifeless.
They hadn’t even realized what had happened.
But the scene didn’t end there. Something even stranger happened.
The five corpses suddenly began sliding across the ground.
Then—
Whoosh!
All five bodies, along with their severed heads, were pulled toward the golden blade in the person’s hand.
The weapon was unlike any ordinary sword.
Its blade had been forged from pure cosmic energy.
The corpses were gradually swallowed into it.
One after another.
Until—
Nothing remained.
Every trace of the five beasts had been completely devoured by the sword.
Then, from the small circular mouth embedded in the hilt—positioned just above the handle and directly beneath the blade—
"Burp." The tiny mouth let out a satisfied burp.
It then slowly closed.
The strange mouth disappeared, leaving behind nothing more than what appeared to be an ordinary red-colored spherical object attached to the sword’s hilt.
"Huh?" The person stared at it in confusion.
He reached out and touched the red sphere again.
Nothing happened.
The mouth didn’t appear.
Instead—
Something else came.
[DING!]
[Congratulations, Luke!]
Paragon’s Judgment has successfully broken its first seal!
[SSS-Rank Growth Artifact]
[Output Limit Increased]
G-Rank → F-Rank
A portion of the sword’s sealed power has been released.
[Elemental Manifestation — Upgraded]
[Elemental Judgment — Upgraded]
[Affinity Synchronization — Upgraded]
New elemental power can now be manifested at F-Rank.
[New Ability detected, click here to see.]

chapters.title: Chapter 284: Two Huge Unlocks in a Single Moment! [GOLDEN TICKET AND POWER STONE BONUS - ]
paragraphs: Yes, the person was Luke.
And the confusion on his face quickly turned into complete delight. After reading seeing this.
As for the clean cuts from earlier—
That hadn’t been because the sword itself was sharp enough to slice through Peak D-Rank bodies.
Luke had relied on Physical Severance authority, while using G-Rank Paragon’s Judgment to create those perfect cuts.
Without it, his current sword wouldn’t have been capable of such an effortless result.
In fact, the weapon was already on the verge of breaking.
After all, he had just used a G-Rank sword to kill a Peak D-Rank being.
And on top of that, he had even used an Authority through it.
Cracks had already spread across the golden blade.
"I need to rank it up more." Luke’s expression became slightly worried as he looked at the damaged weapon.
Fortunately, the sword could repair itself by absorbing energy.
And Luke was already supplying it with energy.
Crack... crack...
The fractures across the blade began closing almost immediately.
Even if the sword were to completely shatter, it wouldn’t truly be lost.
The weapon was connected to his soul, meaning it would eventually reappear.
The only problem would be the huge amount of energy required to restore it.
But then Luke’s expression suddenly changed.
His eyes narrowed.
"Wait a minute." The moment the G-Rank seal broke, Paragon’s Judgment had advanced to F-Rank.
Luke’s mind immediately connected the dots.
Those five Peak D-Rank beasts...
All of them together had only provided enough energy to break the G-Rank seal.
"A Body Temper realm seal?" The corner of Luke’s mouth twitched.
He could already imagine the amount of energy required for the next breakthrough.
It was going to be absurd.
Still, despite the thought of that expenditure, Luke couldn’t suppress his excitement.
At least he had discovered another path for the sword’s growth.
Before this, his only real method had been slowly allowing it to grow by countering different elemental powers.
Now, however, he had discovered that the sword could also advance by consuming other beings.
That was undoubtedly good news.
The problem was—
He had no idea how much energy the next seal would require.
"Whatever." Luke shook his head, putting the matter aside for the moment.
First, he needed to make sure there wasn’t any danger nearby.
He carefully scanned his surroundings.
Nothing.
Only darkness stretched through the enormous pathways.
Yet Luke could see through it without difficulty because of his Void affinity.
His gaze eventually settled on the massive walls surrounding the pathway.
The walls extended all the way upward, connecting seamlessly with the ceiling and completely sealing the passage.
Luke stared at them for a moment.
’Can I break them?’ The thought amused him.
But he already knew the answer.
"No."
Otherwise, the knights who had entered these ruins before, especially when they had been traveling together, would have already done exactly that.
So there was no point wasting time thinking about it.
After confirming that there was no immediate threat and finding nothing but silence stretching through the dark pathways, Luke finally relaxed.
With a thought—
A chair made entirely from cosmic energy appeared beside him from his spatial ring.
It was the same cosmic chair he had crafted earlier using Elythos’ armor ability.
Luke casually sat down.
"Sadly, my Nexus Titan doesn’t allow me to freely use every armor ability without actually summoning the armor." Luke sighed.
Although his Nexus Titan allowed him to use armor abilities even while wearing a different set of armor, there were still limitations.
Still, that didn’t stop him from wanting more.
The more abilities he could access without relying on a specific Titan, the better.
’I need more.’
[So greedy.] The System suddenly appeared, casually taunting him.
Luke completely ignored it.
He had long since become accustomed to the System’s occasional teasing.
Instead, his attention shifted toward something far more important.
The newly unlocked ability of Paragon’s Judgment.
[ NEW ABILITY UNLOCKED ]
■ Elemental Barrage
Type: Offensive / Ranged
Rank: F-Rank
Classification: Sword Technique
Description:
Paragon’s Judgment releases condensed elemental energy with every sword swing, transforming each slash into multiple elemental projectiles.
Rather than creating a single ranged attack, the sword fragments the manifested elemental energy into dozens of smaller blades that travel toward the target at high speed.
Effects:
• Each sword swing releases multiple elemental blades.
• All projectiles inherit the sword’s currently manifested element.
• Projectiles can be fired in multiple directions simultaneously.
• Higher elemental control increases projectile accuracy and stability.
• The number and power of projectiles depend on the wielder’s output.
• Multiple projectiles can strike the same target or spread across an area.
• Effective for suppressing groups of enemies and overwhelming defensive positions.
Limitation:
The ability consumes additional energy for every projectile created. Greater projectile numbers result in lower individual power.
"Damn, that’s so OP!" Luke couldn’t help but exclaim after reading through the description.
And this wasn’t even an ability similar to anything he already possessed.
That alone made him even more excited.
"With this, I’ll have far more options in close combat, especially when dealing with multiple enemies."
Luke’s mind immediately began analyzing its applications.
Normally, he relied heavily on overwhelming destructive power and raw physical strength.
Those methods were extremely effective, but they had also left his basic combat style somewhat lacking.
This ability changed that.
First, it gave him another way to attack without relying purely on brute force.
Second, he could catch his enemies off guard and land several additional attacks before they even understood what was happening.
"Even though the current limit is only ten projectiles, that’s still plenty."
As he muttered those words, Luke’s imagination had already begun running wild.
He could already picture himself launching a single attack—
And then an entire sky filled with swords appearing above his enemies.
Before raining down upon them all at once.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Just imagining the scene made Luke’s blood boil with excitement.
After all, who didn’t want a ridiculously cool trick like that?
"Yeah, Cosmic Punch is powerful and all..." Luke nodded.
"But this looks way cooler."
His grin widened as he imagined the expressions of his enemies.
Their faces would probably turn pale the moment they looked up and saw an entire sky filled with swords pointed directly at them.
Just thinking about it made him even more eager.
"So I need to break more seals as quickly as possible."
With that decision made, Luke prepared to continue his hunt.
But before he could move—
Ding!
Another notification appeared.
Luke’s expression immediately soured.
’Seriously? What is the System trying to do now?’
At first, he found the sudden interruption annoying. And thought, system was just annoying him.
But the moment he actually read the notification—
His irritation vanished and his eyes widened along with his expression changed completely.
Then, with the utmost sincerity, Luke clasped his hands together. And prayed to goddess of luck.
"Please, bless your most devoted follower, my Goddess."
The System couldn’t help itself.
If it had been able to speak at that moment, it would have definitely mocked him.
[Most devoted? Heh!]
Unfortunately, it couldn’t.
So instead, it simply continued displaying the notification.
And the notification was—
[CONGRATULATIONS, LUKE! YOUR FOURTH TITAN SUMMON IS NOW AVAILABLE!]
[SUMMON NOW?]

Then, with the utmost sincerity, Luke clasped his hands together.
And prayed to goddess of luck.
"Please, bless your most devoted follower, my Goddess."
The System couldn’t help itself.
If it had been able to speak at that moment, it would have definitely mocked him.
[Most devoted?
Heh!]
Unfortunately, it couldn’t.
So instead, it simply continued displaying the notification.
And the notification was—
[CONGRATULATIONS, LUKE!
YOUR FOURTH TITAN SUMMON IS NOW AVAILABLE!]
[SUMMON NOW?]

chapters.title: Chapter 285: The Forbidden Titan the Cosmos Tried to Erase
paragraphs: "Fourth Titan is finally here!" Luke exclaimed excitedly.
After waiting for so long, the moment had finally arrived.
He didn’t waste even a second before choosing to summon it.
"Let’s see what I’ll get." With that, Luke pressed the summon button.
This time, there was no gacha-like result.
Instead, the System began pre-loading information about the Titan.
[Loading...]

It was actually a useful feature the System had introduced since his previous summonings, allowing him to receive the Titan’s information immediately rather than having to wait for everything to appear after titan summoned.
Luke watched the loading window with growing anticipation.
Then—
DING!
A long information window unfolded before him, filling his vision with the complete description of the Crypt Titan.
[SPECIES: CRYPT TITAN]
Classification: Forbidden Titan Species
Nature: Sealing / Containment / Suppression
Origin: Unknown
Known Status: Sealed
Threat Classification: Unmeasurable
[INDIVIDUAL: SEVAROTH]
Status: Firstborn Crypt Titan
Nature: Born Sealed
Core Authority: Sealing
[Description]
Long before civilizations began recording history, the Firstborn Titans started appearing across the Cosmos.

They were extraordinary beings, born with potential that ordinary life could never hope to comprehend. As they matured, their powers developed into Paths, and their understanding of those Paths eventually allowed them to stand beyond the limitations imposed upon lesser beings.
Then Sevaroth was born.
Something went wrong.

The Cosmos sensed it immediately, yet even it could not determine what had happened. There was no trace of the interference afterward. No law could identify its source, and no surviving consciousness remembered witnessing anything unusual.
Whatever had entered the process of Sevaroth’s birth had vanished without leaving an explanation.
Only the result remained.
The newborn existence was something the Cosmos considered dangerous.
It could not allow that being to grow freely.
So the Cosmos created another Titan and used it as a vessel. The original existence was sealed inside, buried beneath countless layers of restrictions that could not be broken from within or outside.
Then history itself was altered.
Records were rewritten. Memories disappeared. Ancient accounts changed without anyone noticing. Even the traces that could have revealed that another existence had once been there were erased.
Eventually, the Cosmos left behind a single version of the truth.
On that day, the Crypt Titan was born.
And that was all anyone remembered.
Sevaroth, however, knew better.

His body had never truly been meant to be his own. It was a prison constructed around something the Cosmos refused to let exist freely. His entire existence had been reduced to containing what lay within him.
So he watched his siblings grow.

He saw them awaken their abilities, discover their Paths, and gradually reach heights that had once seemed impossible. They continued advancing while Sevaroth remained trapped inside the same existence that had been designed for him.
At first, he simply observed.
Eventually, he began to understand what had been done to him.
The Cosmos had not merely weakened him.
It had decided his purpose before he had even opened his eyes.
And that realization made him laugh.
Not because his situation was amusing, but because the solution the Cosmos had chosen was almost absurd.
It had tried to imprison something it feared by creating a vessel around it.
What it had failed to realize was that the vessel could learn.
Sevaroth spent ages studying his own imprisonment.

He examined the restrictions surrounding his existence and slowly understood the principles behind them. He learned how the seals interacted, how power could be restricted, how an existence could be isolated, and how even space itself could be closed off through sealing techniques.
He began reproducing those methods.
What had originally been used against him became the subject of his obsession.

Over an incomprehensible span of time, Sevaroth learned every form of sealing he could discover. He mastered containment, suppression, binding, and the methods required to imprison energy, consciousness, space, and even aspects of existence itself.
Eventually, he reached the extreme of the Path.
And the Cosmos acknowledged him.
He received the title of Warden of the Sealed Path.
Yet even that title was not left untouched.
The moment Sevaroth reached the extreme of the Path, the Cosmos sealed the very Warden Path it had just acknowledged in him.
It was not a reward.
It was mockery.
As if the Cosmos itself was telling him that the Path he had spent eternity mastering was never truly his to begin with.
For a moment, Sevaroth simply stared at the title.
Then he laughed again.
The irony was almost impossible to describe.
The very Path that had been forced upon him was now the one he had mastered beyond the reach of ordinary beings.
Yet it changed nothing.
He still could not free himself.
That was the boundary he could never cross.

The Path of Sealing was not something Sevaroth had originally chosen. It was born from the chains placed around him. His understanding of it could become perfect, but that perfection did not transform it into the innate power he had been denied.
And because of that, Sevaroth encountered the same wall that separated Wardens from those who had gone beyond them.
His brothers and sisters continued their ascent.
They stepped past their Warden Titles and reached heights Sevaroth could only watch from afar.
He remained behind.
Not because he was incapable of mastering a Path.
He had mastered one more completely than almost anyone else could imagine.
The problem was that his greatest Path was also the proof that the Cosmos had succeeded in defining his existence.
That became Sevaroth’s greatest tragedy.
He eventually became the strongest Crypt Titan in existence.
There was no second one.
No other being shared his species, and no successor ever appeared to inherit his name.
Across the entire Cosmos, Sevaroth stood alone.
And despite that distinction, he was still considered one of the weaker members among his Firstborn siblings.
Not because he lacked intelligence.
Not because he lacked determination.
And certainly not because he lacked mastery.
He had simply been denied the freedom that the others were born with.
The Cosmos had given him a prison and forced him to spend eternity becoming its greatest architect.
So Sevaroth continued to search.
Somewhere within the countless seals surrounding his existence remained the being he had once been.
The Cosmos had erased his history.
It had hidden his birth.
It had turned his body into a vessel and buried the truth beneath an age of forgotten records.
But it had never succeeded in making Sevaroth accept his fate.
And somewhere, deep beneath everything the Cosmos had sealed away, the original Sevaroth was still waiting.
A long silence followed.
All of Luke’s excitement from earlier had completely disappeared.
His eyes remained fixed on the description before him, reading about a Titan whose entire existence had been erased from the universe.
A Titan who had been sealed away.
Yet even after being reduced to such a state, he had never surrendered.
Instead, he had turned his own prison into his teacher and learned the forbidden art of sealing from it.
And even then—
The universe had sealed his Warden Path as well.
As if everything he had learned was nothing more than a cruel joke.
A mockery the cosmos itself was making toward that hidden observer.
"But... he still hasn’t given up." Luke muttered those words while slowly releasing a deep breath.
He had never imagined that he would encounter something like this.
Yet it also left him with a question.
"The System has always given me perfect things."
He paused, remembering all the previous rewards and Titans it had given him.
"It has described them as perfect many times."
His brows furrowed.
"So what about this time?" The question slipped from his lips.
Luke was genuinely impressed by Sevaroth.
There was no doubt about that.
But compared to the other Forbidden Titans, Sevaroth was the weakest.
And even worse—
His path itself was flawed.
"So why did the System give me this?" Luke rubbed his chin thoughtfully, his gaze becoming more serious.
Then, after a moment, he decided to stop wondering for now.
"Well, let’s see what he has first." With that, Luke opened Sevaroth’s ability information.

chapters.title: Chapter 286: Why Did the System Choose the “Weakest” Titan?
paragraphs: [DING!]
[According to your current breakthrough, four Sealing Abilities of Sevaroth would be unlocked.]
[1. SEAL OF SUPPRESSION]
Unlock Rank: G-Rank
Description:
Sevaroth places a seal upon a target’s source of power, restricting how much of that power can be accessed.
The seal can target physical strength, mana, aether, an individual ability, a technique, or multiple sources at once. Against sufficiently powerful enemies, it can even interfere with an Authority.
The amount of power affected depends on the energy invested into the seal.
Key Trait:
The target retains the sealed power, but cannot draw upon the restricted portion until the seal is removed or expires.
"Interesting." Luke raised a brow and nodded.
After reading Sevaroth’s history, he had already expected the first ability to be related to sealing.
Still, actually seeing it appear before his eyes was an entirely different feeling.
And honestly—
It looked pretty cool.
More importantly, it filled a gap in Luke’s current arsenal.
When it came to crowd control, he didn’t really have anything particularly effective.
He could use the bindings created through his Cosmic Constructs ability, but those were hardly reliable against the opponents he usually faced.
After all, Luke was constantly fighting beings above his own rank.
Against such enemies, ordinary bindings couldn’t accomplish much.
A sealing ability, however...
That was something different.
"Let’s see the other one as well." With that, Luke shifted his attention to the second seal and checked its ability.
[2. SEAL OF SILENCE]
Unlock Rank: F-Rank
Description:
Sevaroth seals the means through which a target releases power.
The technique can interfere with spellcasting, incantations, voice-based abilities, activation commands, energy projection, and other abilities that require an external manifestation.
The seal can be placed on the hands, throat, or another point involved in the activation process.
Key Trait:
Abilities that remain fully intact inside the target can become impossible to express outwardly.
"Another amazing ability." Luke couldn’t help but praise Sevaroth again after seeing this second seal.
This ability could prevent destruction before it even happened.
Especially against mages and other spellcasters.
If he sealed their mouths, then they wouldn’t even be able to chant or speak their spells.
Without that, those supposedly powerful spellcasters would be reduced to little more than paper mages.
The more he looked at Sevaroth’s abilities, the more surprised Luke became.
"I’m surprisingly finding this Titan more and more interesting." His earlier doubts about Sevaroth had already begun to fade.
With his mood improving, Luke shifted his attention to the next seal.
The third Seal.
[3. SEAL OF RESTRAINT]
Unlock Rank: E-Rank
Description:
Sevaroth creates a binding seal that interferes with the target’s movement.
Once applied, it follows the target regardless of where they move. It can progressively restrict individual limbs before extending its influence across the entire body.
At greater strength, the seal can hinder the circulation of energy required for movement and temporarily immobilize powerful opponents.
Key Trait:
Escaping its original position does not break the seal. It remains attached to the designated target until its duration ends or the seal is destroyed.
"This should be first to appear, but it’s good it came." Luke nodded satisfied and already imagined many scenes where he would use all four seals to make the enemies powerless.
"So, let’s see the fourth and final seal which would unlock."
[4. SEAL OF CLOSURE]
Unlock Rank: D-Rank
Description:
Sevaroth can forcibly shut something that has been opened or is currently maintaining an active connection.
The seal can close dimensional rifts, magical portals, exposed energy channels, activated artifacts, wounds, and transformations that have not yet reached completion.
As Sevaroth’s power develops, the same principle can be applied to increasingly complex connections, including the link between a being and its source of power.
Key Trait:
The seal remains locked until its conditions are fulfilled, making it possible to keep a sealed phenomenon from reopening on its own.
"Awesome!" Luke exclaimed in amazement after reading the description of the final seal.
This one was far more absurd than the previous seals.
And then there was the ability to seal wounds.
That alone made genuine excitement flicker in Luke’s eyes.
Previously, he had no way to heal his own wounds, let alone someone else’s.
"If I had this ability earlier, I could have healed Theia’s external injuries myself." A hint of complaint slipped into his voice.
But Luke quickly shook his head and pushed those unnecessary thoughts away.
There was no point dwelling on something that had already happened.
At that moment, another System screen suddenly appeared before him.
[Did you like it?]
Luke paused.
The message immediately brought the question from earlier back into his mind.
"Why did you choose this?"
He narrowed his eyes slightly. "You know what I mean."
Luke waited for the System’s response.
It wasn’t that he disliked the new Titan.
Quite the opposite.
The truth was, he found Sevaroth’s abilities surprisingly useful and believed that the Crypt Titan would provide him with tremendous help.
Perhaps that was exactly why the System had chosen him.
After all, the System had often given him things when he genuinely needed them.
His previous Titans had also been part of his preparation for the inevitable moment when he would become a true Titan himself.
Even so, the question continued to bother him.
’Why Sevaroth?’ Luke remained lost in thought for a moment.
Then—
The System finally gave him an answer.
[Luke, you are wrong here.]
The System’s words immediately left Luke confused.
He frowned slightly, but didn’t interrupt.
[There is not a single thing in this world that is truly perfect.]
Luke’s expression became serious.
[And the System takes what already exists and makes it perfect.]
[Your Titans are one such example.]
[If both Nyx and you were to reach the peak of the Void Titan, then your Titan form would be perfect.]
[In terms of your natural characteristics alone, you would easily surpass Nyx.]
The System paused briefly before clarifying.
[I am not talking about skills.]
[Anyone has the opportunity to learn skills.]
[That is something entirely different.]
Luke remained silent, listening carefully.
[Think of it this way.]
[Somewhere in the universe, a being may possess a perfection rating of 9 out of 10.]
[Even the greatest creation made by the Universe itself might reach 9.9999... and continue with countless more nines.]
[But it will never reach 10/10.]
The System paused again.
Its next words carried a strange sense of finality.
[But everything the System gives you is a 10 out of 10 at its respective level.]
Luke’s eyes shifted slightly.
[The problem is that you cannot comprehend that perfection.]
[You are not a 10-rated existence yourself.]
[So how could you possibly make perfect use of something that was created at perfection?]
Silence.
Luke didn’t answer immediately.
The meaning behind those words slowly settled into his mind.
The flaw wasn’t in the Titans.
It was in him.
Luke finally released a quiet sigh.
Because, unfortunately—
The System was right.

chapters.title: Chapter 287: The Final Piece That Could Free Sevaroth
paragraphs: Like his Titans, Luke hadn’t understood many things when he first obtained them.
But as he gradually learned more, he had eventually developed Cosmic Punch.
Caelith had helped him along the way, but what Luke ultimately created wasn’t simply Caelith’s Cosmic Punch.
It had become an entirely new version of Cosmic Punch.
So, in the end, his tools had always been perfect.
The problem had never been the tools themselves.
It was that Luke hadn’t yet reached the level where he could use them perfectly.
[That’s why the System will make you a perfect Titan.]
[At the very least, your form will become perfect.]
The System said nothing more after that.
Instead, another notification immediately appeared before Luke.
[MERGE WITH SEVAROTH, THE CRYPT TITAN?]
Luke stared at the screen for several minutes.
His eyes remained fixed on one particular word.
Merge.
Not summon.
"Seems like the System has already started forming the bond."
Luke muttered thoughtfully.
The appearance of the word merge had already given him an idea of what was about to happen.
"So... the fourth Titan’s bloodline is coming now."
His gaze drifted upward toward the dark ceiling.
He couldn’t help but remember the immense pain from his previous integration.
The agony and also the coma-like state that had followed.
"Would the same thing happen again?" So he asked the System directly.
[No.]
[You are a real Titan now.]
[So this time, you will only lose consciousness for a few hours.]
Luke blinked.
"A few hours..." That was considerably better than before.
Still, he wasn’t going to underestimate it.
"Then I have to make some preparations."
With that, Luke immediately summoned Elythos’ armor.
At the same time, his body began transforming.
Cosmic energy surged through him as he took on the form of the Cosmic Heart Titan.
His body quickly reached its full size—
Twenty feet tall.
The same size as his Void Titan form.
Then Luke began constructing a thick, sturdy sphere around himself.
He made sure it was strong enough that, during the time he would be unconscious, nothing nearby could easily destroy it.
And even if something did manage to break through its defenses, it would still need considerable time to do so.
A few minutes later, a massive sphere had finally taken shape.
It stood fifty feet tall and fifty feet wide, attached firmly to one side of the wall.
Luke had intentionally placed it there, leaving plenty of open space around it.
That way, even if something somehow decided to attack the sphere and failed to break through it, they would eventually grow tired and leave after wasting enough time.
"Wait a second." Just as Luke was about to enter, an important question suddenly came to his mind.
"What about my clones?" His expression became worried.
"What will happen to them?
He didn’t want his clones to disappear again like they had before.
That alone could create far too many problems.
Fortunately, the System’s next response immediately reassured him.
[Don’t worry. Your clones are real Titans as well, and their connection with your Void affinity means they will not disappear.]
[However, they will also lose consciousness.]
[The main Luke is still you, after all.]
[So when you merge with the fourth Titan, the fusion will affect all realities—including your clones.]
[However, the main effect will appear on your body first before gradually spreading to theirs.]
"Okay." Reassured, Luke gave his four clones an order to find suitable places and rest.
Once that was done, he returned to his normal Titan form and stepped inside the newly constructed sphere.
"I am ready." Luke lay down upon the hard cosmic material.
Despite its appearance, the surface wasn’t particularly uncomfortable against his body.
He slowly relaxed.
Then—
[See you in a few hours.] The System’s final words carried its usual cheeky tone.
After that, numerous notifications immediately began appearing before Luke.
But he never got the chance to see them.
His consciousness had already slipped away into a deep sleep.
[System: Initiating synchronization with Sevaroth, the Crypt Titan.]
[Preparing Origin Core...]
[Preparing Titan Essence...]
[Establishing connection...]
[Sealing interference detected...]
[Recalculating...]
[Beginning Titan Merge...]
Meanwhile, somewhere within an endless prison, a colossal being slept peacefully.
His body was so enormous that it could easily be described as the size of a galaxy.
He was bound by dozens of chains, just like his brothers and sisters.
Yet there was something strange about him.
He wasn’t struggling against them.
He simply slept... peacefully.
As though those chains weren’t truly imprisoning him at all. But instead he had willingly chosen to remain there.
His physique was heavily muscular, and if his body were somehow reduced to the size of an ordinary human, his build would still appear extremely imposing.
His skin was dark grey, while enormous dark-black rings encircled both his wrists and ankles.
From each of those four rings, thick chains extended outward.
But instead of disappearing into the darkness, they traveled back toward his body and connected directly to his chest.
There, embedded in the center of his chest, was a strange sphere resembling a green, necrotic flame.
The chains were connected to that sphere.
And then there was his head.
His entire head was concealed beneath a massive helmet.
The helmet was covered in spikes, while its front possessed bars arranged like a mask.
Its entire surface was an iron-grey color.
From the openings of the helmet, faint green smoke continuously escaped.
Yet even if someone somehow managed to look through the barred front—
They would see nothing.
Only endless darkness.
It was as though whatever existed inside the helmet couldn’t be seen at all.
The chains binding his body extended further outward, disappearing into the void itself.
That was what kept his enormous body fixed in place.
And behind him rested a massive coffin.
It was completely crimson-red, with an eerie flame-like crimson glow flickering across its surface.
That was his armor.
Surprisingly, it hadn’t been granted to him by the Universe.
After all, every Titan created their own armor themselves.
But for some unknown reason, he had chosen to make his armor in the shape of a coffin.
No one knew why.
However, the tranquility that had already been broken three times was shattered once again.
This time, though, it wasn’t another forbidden ritual.
Instead, something far simpler appeared.
An offer.
[The final piece, which would free you.]
That was all it took.
Sevaroth’s eyes suddenly opened.
Of course, no one could see them, as his entire head remained hidden behind the iron-grey helmet.
He slowly looked around, trying to locate the source of the voice—or whatever being had spoken to him.
But there was nothing.
Then Sevaroth noticed something else.
His three siblings were gone.
"Where have they gone?" Confusion appeared in his voice as he looked toward the places where they had once been.
Then the earlier words surfaced in his mind.
’The final piece...’
"Seems like it is." A smile formed across his face, although the helmet concealed it completely.
"Then let’s see what this final piece is." The moment those words left his mouth—
The massive coffin behind him suddenly moved.
It had remained firmly closed until now, tightly wrapped in chains.
Then, without warning—
The coffin’s eyes opened. And so did its mouth.
The next instant, all the chains binding the coffin were violently sucked inside it.
Whoosh!
The chains wrapped around Sevaroth’s body were pulled away as well, disappearing into the coffin one after another.
Only the four enormous rings remained.
The chains connected to the green, necrotic sphere embedded within his chest also remained untouched.
Those were different.
They had been created by the Cosmos itself.
And even Sevaroth didn’t bother trying to remove them.
He simply moved.
The massive coffin behind him shifted into position as he stepped forward.
Then, with the coffin accompanying him, Sevaroth opened a portal.
Without another word, he stepped through it.
His destination—
Luke.
