chapters.title: Chapter 296: Ten Platinum Knights and a Mysterious Stranger! [POWER STONE BONUS - ]
paragraphs: "Hahaha!"

Ivar broke into a sadistic laugh, already certain that Luke was about to die. Once that happened, he could turn his attention back to Isaria, devour her life force along with her ability, and use the stolen power to replenish the lifespan he had sacrificed.
At least, that was the future he had already envisioned.
Unfortunately for him, a mocking voice cut through his laughter.
"You... call this... a star?"
Luke looked at the black sphere above Ivar’s palm with a mocking smile before slowly shaking his head.
"Let me show you what a real star is."
As soon as those words fell, Luke casually raised one hand.
The empty space high above and diagonally behind him suddenly trembled.
Then, without any warning, a gigantic red sphere materialized.
Its diameter reached an astonishing one kilometer.

The moment it appeared, brilliant light flooded the entire pathway, banishing the darkness that had filled the ancient maze for who knew how long. The sudden radiance was so intense that even cracks created earlier in the dark walls became clearly visible.
The monsters and beasts hiding throughout the surrounding pathways reacted immediately.
They fled.

Some scrambled deeper into the darkness, while others desperately moved away from the terrifying light. After spending countless years in an environment where darkness was the norm, this sudden brightness was something they had never experienced before.
"This is called a star." Luke spoke casually, seemingly oblivious to the expression on Ivar’s face.
Ivar could only stare at the enormous red sphere with his mouth hanging open.
"It’s not... a fireball."
His voice trembled slightly as the realization sank in.
"It’s a star."
Earlier, in the plaza, Luke had deliberately kept the sphere’s heat and gravitational force suppressed, so Ivar hadn’t been able to truly sense what stood before him.
Now, however, even a small portion of that power had been released.
The heat alone was terrifying.
It was nothing like the heat produced by an ordinary fireball.
The difference was so enormous that calling Luke’s creation a fireball almost felt insulting.
’Sir Luke is so strong...’
Isaria stared at the enormous red sphere with shining eyes, her earlier fear momentarily forgotten as admiration filled her heart.
Beside her, Kiki tilted its coffin-shaped body upward and nodded repeatedly.
"Kiki."
The little coffin seemed completely proud of its master, as though agreeing wholeheartedly with Isaria.
’My master really is amazing.’
Meanwhile, with the red star suspended behind him, Luke turned his gaze toward the front-right side of the pathway, where a distant junction could be seen connecting several dark passages.
"I thought my red star would make you afraid, but it seems I was wrong."
His voice carried through the maze and reached the distant junction.
Nothing happened.
Only an eerie silence remained.

Ivar and Isaria became confused, before immediately using their respective abilities to search the area. Their enhanced owl eyes swept across the distant pathways, walls, and every possible hiding place, yet neither could detect a single presence.
Luke noticed their confusion but didn’t bother explaining.
His eyes remained fixed on that junction.
The distance between them was 1.5 kilometers.
Yes, a full 1.5 kilometers.
Normally, even that distance would have made detecting someone extremely difficult.
But Luke’s perception had changed considerably after obtaining the Crown of Void.

When he had first acquired the Void halo, it had granted him a passive ability that prevented anything within a fifty-meter radius from concealing itself from him. In other words, anything within a total diameter of one hundred meters couldn’t escape his perception unless it possessed a way to hide from the Void itself.
That limitation, however, disappeared after he became a Real Titan.
The ability merged with Luke’s basic energy-control range, which had continued expanding alongside his cultivation.
At the Bronze Knight realm, his energy-control area had only covered a diameter of one hundred meters.
Now, it had reached an entire one-kilometer diameter.
With the Crown of Void active, nothing within that range could remain hidden from him.
As for why Ivar and Isaria hadn’t been able to detect them, Luke already had a possible explanation.
Maybe because of distance.
Or maybe, their abilities probably aren’t strong enough to see through whatever method those guys are using to conceal themselves.
His guess wasn’t without reason.
After the fusion, the range of his Void halo had also increased, causing his previous one-kilometer detection diameter to expand to two kilometers.
And Luke was right.

Isaria possessed an ability that allowed her to perceive almost anything hidden from ordinary senses. However, even that ability had a range limit. More importantly, she was only at the C-Rank, while the beings hiding ahead were stronger than her.
That difference alone, combined with their concealment method, was enough to keep them beyond her perception.
Before Ivar and Isaria could think any further about the situation, a slow clapping sound suddenly echoed from the very junction Luke had been watching.
Clap. Clap. Clap.
"Impressive, Hero of Light."
The voice praised Luke.
But he remained silent.
Ivar and Isaria, however, were left stunned.
Both possessed abilities capable of detecting things that ordinary senses couldn’t even perceive, yet neither had noticed the hidden presence.
Luke had.
And what made it even more surprising was that they had never known him to possess such terrifying perception.
As the realization settled in, a black-robed figure finally stepped out from the distant junction.
His entire body was concealed beneath the robe, leaving his appearance completely hidden.
But he wasn’t alone.
Ten more people emerged behind him.
Unlike the black-robed man, however, these ten were dressed in the uniforms of the Sunborn Royal Palace.
Ivar and Isaria immediately recognized them.
They were among the hundred B-Rank warriors who had entered the ruins alongside them.
Ten Platinum Knights.
"Seems like some rats have entered the Eldric Kingdom."
Luke said it playfully, without even bothering to take the ten Platinum Knights seriously.
His attention remained fixed entirely on the black-robed man standing behind them.
That was the only one who caught Luke’s interest.
He couldn’t sense his true strength at all.
The black-robed man didn’t seem offended by the remark. Instead, he calmly replied with a faint smile.
"You’re wrong, Hero of Light."
His gaze then shifted toward the massive red star hovering behind Luke.
For a moment, a trace of approval appeared in his eyes as he examined it. But that expression quickly turned strange when something else caught his attention.
In the distance, Kiki was happily chewing on a long bone.
What made the sight bizarre wasn’t the bone itself, but the way the little coffin was eating it.
Its coffin lid was opening and closing as it gnawed away, rather than using the mouth on the front of its coffin.
The black-robed man’s expression twitched slightly.
He stared for another moment before finally deciding it was better to ignore whatever that thing was and returned his attention to Luke.
"We aren’t rats."
His voice became colder.
"Our god’s companion, once entered this place and slaughtered every fake god who lived here."
Luke was slightly stunned.
He hadn’t expected such a revelation to come so suddenly.
Yet the black-robed man continued as though Luke’s reaction didn’t matter.
"We intended to deal with you later, because a Hero is always an anomaly."
His expression twitched faintly as an unpleasant memory surfaced in his mind.
Whatever had happened in the past clearly wasn’t something he remembered fondly.
"Thanks, I guess."
Luke’s playful reply instantly pulled him out of those memories.
The black-robed man’s expression twitched again.
He gave Luke a slightly irritated look-one that hadn’t been there before.
The black-robed man then turned his attention toward Ivar.

The Dead Star continued pulsing above his palm, but its price was now impossible to ignore. The young prince who had appeared moments ago had already aged dramatically, his skin withered and his body reduced to the appearance of a two-hundred-year-old mummy.
"But Sir Ivar is an important member of our organization. For his protection, I had to reveal myself."
With that, he finally disclosed the real reason he had stepped forward.
Luke raised a brow at the revelation before giving a small nod.
"Well, Ivar is a prince. Having two or three memberships in secret organizations is pretty normal."
He nodded as though that conclusion made perfect sense.
However, the moment the black-robed man spoke again, he took his words back.
"Our Demon Whisper organization."
"The Infernal Choir!"
The man’s declaration echoed through the dark pathway.
Luke’s mouth twitched.
Because, he had encountered three princes so far if the human prince was included, and now he had learned that two of them belonged to this very same Demon Whisper organization.
Thinking this, he felt that even the human prince was also part of this, it was just he didn’t get any chance to show his entry.
’Concentrate, Luke.’
He quickly pushed the useless thought aside and looked toward Ivar instead.
Ivar’s expression had turned extremely ugly.
Clearly, he had never intended for this secret to be exposed.
The black-robed man noticed his reaction and let out a faint, amused smile.
"Sir Ivar, what are you afraid of?"
His gaze shifted toward Luke.
"Soon, this Hero will be dead. And everyone else inside these ruins will die with him."
His smile widened.
"So don’t worry. Your secret will remain safe."

chapters.title: Chapter 297: They Came for the Princesses—But Found Luke!
paragraphs: "What did you say?" Luke’s playful smile disappeared.

The amusement that had been present in his eyes was gone, replaced by a cold, steady gaze that made it clear Marrec had touched upon something Luke considered far more important than the man could have known.

Hearing those words, Marrec didn’t replied, instead. He reached up and removed the black robe that had concealed his face and body before throwing it onto the ground beside him. The robe fell in a heap, revealing the black leather armor covering his body.
However, it was his face that drew Isaria’s attention.
"This?"
Isaria’s hands immediately covered her mouth, and her eyes widened as she stared at him.
Marrec’s face had changed, but not completely.
Instead, it looked as though two different existences had been divided across it. One side remained human, with familiar facial features, while the other had taken on a distinctly demonic appearance.

Darker skin stretched across the corrupted side, following the sharply defined shape of his cheekbone and jaw. A crimson eye glowed from within it, while a short black horn curved upward from his forehead above the eye. Thin demonic markings extended outward from the crimson eye and spread across his cheek before disappearing beneath his neck.
The changes weren’t limited to his face either.
Demonic claws had appeared on his hands, while patches of black scales covered portions of his body.
It was a characteristic transformation of the Infernal Choir.

As their members advanced through the realms, their bodies gradually began to change alongside their increasing power, and the further they progressed, the more apparent those demonic characteristics became.
There was even a rumor that, at the highest levels, the members of the Infernal Choir would completely transform into demon species.
For Isaria, seeing such a transformation so close was naturally disturbing.
Ivar, however, barely reacted.
He had already seen several higher-ranking members of the organization, and some of their physical transformations had been far more severe than Marrec’s current appearance.
Luke was even less affected.
After becoming a Titan, there were very few things that could genuinely disturb him on a psychological level.
"Allow me to introduce myself, oh, Hero of Light."
Marrec’s voice remained calm as he looked toward Luke, apparently enjoying the opportunity to finally reveal himself.
"Marrec, a Black Chorus of the Infernal Choir."
Luke didn’t respond.
He simply listened, keeping the anger that had surfaced earlier under control.
Marrec continued without seeming bothered by Luke’s silence.
"Our god, Iveron, Demon God of Infernal Flame, wants your sacrifice."
His crimson eye flickered slightly as he spoke.
"Sadly, we failed last time in Stormveil County."
There was a strange confidence in his tone, as though the failure of their previous plan was nothing more than a minor setback.
"So, we tried another method."
He paused briefly.
"Or... another sacrifice."
A smile slowly spread across his face, making his already disturbing half-demonic appearance seem even more sinister.
"If not the hero, then a royal sacrifice will do."
Marrec let those words linger for a moment before glancing toward the surrounding dark walls.
"Which leads us here, where a Vampire Princess and two king-tier bloodline princesses are present."
His gaze returned to Luke, and the sinister smile on his face widened.
"But we never expected that you, a hero, would also come here by yourself."
He gave a quiet chuckle.
"It seems even our god’s will has brought you here."
"Hahaha!"
His laughter echoed through the dark passage, and the more he thought about the situation, the more pleased he became.

He had never expected Luke to appear here on his own, but his unexpected arrival only made the situation better for them. If everything went according to plan, the presence of the Hero of Light would only further accelerate their god’s awakening.
Marrec’s laughter continued for another moment before Luke’s voice cut through it.
"Are you done?"
The words were spoken without any particular force, yet they were enough to make Marrec’s laughter stop.
His smile remained on his face, although it became slightly stiff as he stared at Luke.
Ivar also looked toward Luke with a strange expression.
Marrec was a mid-B-rank, yet Luke was standing there and provoking him as though he didn’t understand the difference between them.
If Marrec truly became enraged, Luke’s death would only become more painful.
’Arrogance.’ Ivar mocked him inwardly.
Earlier...
Inside Luke’s mind, however, something entirely different was happening.
’They want to harm Selene.’
That single thought was enough to stir anger within him.
He wanted to tear Marrec apart.
He wanted to destroy everyone who had any intention of harming Selene.
The emotion was genuine, but Luke had already noticed something wrong with it.
The chains binding his hearts had begun contracting tightly around them.
The chains seemed to be responding to his emotions, attempting to influence his decision and push him toward a particular course of action.

Fortunately, his Titan bloodline reacted before that influence could grow stronger. The mysterious symbols surrounding the chains also moved, suppressing the contraction around his hearts and removing the unnatural pressure.
’This again.’ Luke sighed inwardly.
It wasn’t that he hadn’t been angry when Marrec threatened his wife.
He had.
That anger was his own.

What Luke didn’t want was for some goddess to interfere with his emotions and force them in a particular direction. If he became furious, he wanted that fury to come from himself rather than from an emotion that had been artificially intensified.
’Why did she do this?’ So, this question surfaced in his mind again.
Unfortunately, the system had never given him an answer, while he had no way of meeting the goddess herself and asking her directly.
At least, not now.
Luke had already considered several possibilities on his own, but he couldn’t be certain whether any of them were actually correct.
If Astron Stellara, Rhaenyra’s father, would here his thoughts. Then he would say only one thing.
"What’s going on in a god’s mind, a mortal could never find."
Current time...
"Are you done?"
The moment those words left Luke’s mouth, Marrec’s laughter stopped.
Ivar was still mocking Luke inwardly, but before that thought could continue more further, something changed.
His eyes widened.
The world seemed to spin around him.
His vision shifted, and when it finally settled, he saw something that his mind struggled to comprehend.
His own body was still standing.
But it had no head.
One hand remained raised, continuing to hold the dead star, which was roughly one meter in diameter.
And behind the headless body stood a figure that had appeared without warning.
It was twenty feet tall.
The figure looked unmistakably like Luke, dressed entirely in black, while a black sword rested casually above its shoulder.

sentences.text: "What did you say?" Luke’s playful smile disappeared.

It was a characteristic transformation of the Infernal Choir.

As their members advanced through the realms, their bodies gradually began to change alongside their increasing power, and the further they progressed, the more apparent those demonic characteristics became.
There was even a rumor that, at the highest levels, the members of the Infernal Choir would completely transform into demon species.

Ivar, however, barely reacted.

A smile slowly spread across his face, making his already disturbing half-demonic appearance seem even more sinister.

chapters.title: Chapter 298: Luke Finally Use Fourth Titan Ability!
paragraphs: There wasn’t even a trace of blood on the blade.
Yet Ivar knew exactly what had happened.
That figure had just beheaded him.
’I am dead.’
The realization came with a strange clarity.
Even while his life was disappearing, his pupils dilated as his mind tried to understand how it had happened.
He hadn’t sensed the giant’s arrival.
He hadn’t seen it move.
One moment, nothing had been behind him.
The next, his B-rank body had already been separated from his head.
Of course, Ivar knew that he had already weakened himself by consuming his life force, leaving him in his weakest state.
But even so, that shouldn’t have been enough to explain what had just happened.
How had Luke’s clone appeared without warning?
How had it crossed the distance?
And how had it cut through his B-rank body so easily?
Before those questions could linger any longer, Ivar noticed the giant raising one hand toward the dead star still hovering above his palm.
The giant’s lips moved.
Ivar couldn’t hear the words clearly. But it whispered.
’2nd Seal: Seal of Silence.’
Next instant, a thin white-gold silk thread emerged from the giant’s fingers.
It was so fine that it was almost difficult to see, but it moved with incredible precision as it wrapped around the dead star.
One loop followed another.
In an instant, the white-gold thread had completely covered the one-meter-wide dead star, sealing the object from every direction.
And suprisingly, the dead star, didn’t struggle against the sealing power or attempt to escape.
Instead, it remained completely still, almost as though it were willingly allowing the seal to take effect.
Then—
Whoosh!
The dead star disappeared.
At the same time, the white-gold silk shrank down until it became nothing more than a small thread between the giant’s fingers.
The final light in Ivar’s eyes finally dimmed.
Along with his vision darkened.
And with that, the prince of the Demi-Owl Kingdom died.
Meanwhile, Marrec was still trying to process Luke’s earlier arrogance.
’Why is this hero acting so cocky even though he knows that he, his wife, his friend, and everyone else here are going to di—’
However, next moment, his thought suddenly stopped.
His mid-B-rank senses caught movement from the corner of his eye.
A figure had materialized behind the smiling Ivar.
It seemed to have emerged from the darkness.
Or perhaps from the void itself.
’Space teleportation?’
Marrec immediately remembered the rumors surrounding Luke’s clone and his spatial abilities.
So, his thoughts connected the pieces almost instantly.
Then his attention fell upon the black blade rising behind Ivar.
The second Luke was about to strike.
’Not on my watch.’
Marrec’s body tensed as he prepared to launch himself toward the second Luke and knock him away.
To an ordinary person, the scene was happening too quickly to perceive.
For Marrec, however, it was different.
As a mid-B-rank, his reaction speed was already far beyond that of an ordinary person, and it was roughly five times greater than that of an average B-rank.
Because of that, the movement seemed comparatively slow from his perspective.
Outside, however, only a few fractions of a second had passed.
The second Luke had barely raised his sword.
Marrec was already preparing to move.
But before he could even take a step, something happened that was faster than his reaction.
The forty-foot-tall Luke, currently in his VOIDHEART TITAN form, used his ability as well.
’Third Seal: Seal of Restraint.’
As the ability activated, fifty percent of Luke’s energy was consumed.
Before Marrec could react, four black-golden shackles appeared around his wrists and ankles.
"What—"
He didn’t even have time to finish the word.
When, black-golden chains erupted from each shackle and shot toward the ground.
Yet the moment they reached the surface, something strange happened.
The chains passed straight through it.
There was no crack.
No hole.
Not even the slightest mark.
Marrec’s expression changed.
Those chains weren’t simply attaching themselves to the ground.
They were binding the space occupied by the ground itself.
Whatever the exact principle behind the ability was, the result was obvious.
Marrec immediately exerted his strength and tried to pull himself free.
His muscles tightened.
The surrounding air seemed to tremble slightly from the force.
Yet his body didn’t move.
The shackles remained firmly in place, and the more force he applied, the tighter the chains became around his limbs.
That brief restraint was enough.
Right in front of Marrec’s eyes, Ivar’s head separated completely from his body.
The ten Platinum Knights weren’t fast enough to interfere either.
They were even slower than Marrec, and by the time they could properly react, Ivar had already been killed.
The second Luke calmly sealed away the dead star as well.
For a brief moment, silence filled the dark passage.
The bodies remained where they were, while the last traces of movement seemed to disappear from the surroundings.
Then Marrec’s anger exploded.
"HOW DARE YOU!"
His eyes turned bloodshot as his mid-B-rank aura erupted from his body.
BOOM!
The pressure burst outward.
The ten nearby Platinum Knights were caught directly in it and blasted backward, their bodies slamming into the dark walls surrounding the pathway.
Bam!
Bam!
Bam!
Bam!
One after another, their bodies collided with the walls.
The shockwave was considerably stronger than Luke had expected.
He immediately realized that his one-kilometer Void Horizon layer wouldn’t be enough to completely absorb the force unless he expanded the stretched distance by supplying additional energy.
But there was no time.
The shockwave was already approaching him.
Luke immediately created a cosmic system inside and even pulled the red star outside into his body.
Then, using the cosmic system together with his Void Horizon, he braced himself and took the incoming force.
Head-on.
BANG!
The shockwave slammed into his body with the force of a gigantic cannon round.
’Damn.’
Luke cursed inwardly.
He had concentrated his cosmic system around his chest, which meant that he hadn’t supplied enough strength to his legs to keep himself firmly anchored.
Which results, the force pushed him backward slightly, then it increase and when it finally reached peak...
BAM!
His body blasted backward, before getting crashed into the dark wall behind him.
"Sir Luke!"
Isaria’s worried voice immediately reached him.
Fortunately, she had been standing farther away, and Kiki had already shielded her with his coffin-like body.
A few remnant shockwaves reached them afterward, but they had already lost most of their strength by then, leaving Isaria unharmed.
"Ugh, this sucks." Luke’s annoyed voice came from the wall.
A moment later, he pushed himself away from it and stood upright.
Apart from some dust clinging to his clothes, he looked fine.
"Thank god."
Isaria released the breath she had been holding, her tense expression finally easing when she saw Luke stand up as though the collision had barely affected him.
Luke, meanwhile, glanced toward the red-eyed Marrec with an annoyed expression.
’Next time, I need to focus on my legs too.’
"HAH!"
Marrec suddenly shouted.
The next moment, both of his hands began changing.
Luke’s expression became strange.
’The hell...’
Marrec’s hands hadn’t simply caught fire.

The flesh itself had transformed, taking on a glowing magma-like appearance. They looked as though molten material had replaced his hands, yet they remained in their original shape without burning away.
Marrec clenched his fingers and pulled with tremendous force.
The black-golden shackles around his hands immediately strained.
Crack!
A fracture appeared across one of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 299: The Real Name of the Ancient Ruins Is Revealed!
paragraphs: Another crack followed.
Then the shackles shattered.
The magma-like transformation disappeared from his hands, which returned to normal.
Next, his legs underwent the same transformation.
Molten energy flowed across them, turning them into magma-like limbs while retaining their original shape.
Marrec planted his feet and pulled once again.
Crack!
The shackles around his ankles shattered as well.
"Well, there goes my fifty percent energy."
Seeing this, Luke could only sigh.
It wasn’t that he was disappointed in the seal.
Quite the opposite.
The Seal of Restraint had performed remarkably well, especially considering that Marrec was a mid-B-rank and had been forced to use a special transformation merely to break free.
And there was another advantage.
’I am the Voidheart Titan, meaning I don’t lack either Void or cosmic energy.’
A faint smile appeared on Luke’s face.
With that, his Cosmic Heart immediately began pumping more energy throughout his body, replenishing his reserves at an extremely rapid pace.
After the fusion, he could even generate the energy of his other Titans through the Cosmic Heart.
Like currently, he could also generate void energy.
That had been impossible before.
Unfortunately, the Nexus Titan ability still had a limitation.
It allowed him to use the abilities of his other Titans regardless of the form he was currently using, but it didn’t grant him their inherent characteristics.
In other words, if Luke wanted to directly control Void energy, he still had to transform into the Void Titan.
Otherwise, he could use the abilities he already possessed, but he couldn’t simply gain basic Void elemental control.
’Maybe my Nexus Titan hasn’t fully developed yet.’
Luke considered the possibility.
’Or maybe it’s related to my Titan Knight Origin Skill.’
He was still thinking about it when Marrec’s voice pulled him back to the present.
"You have called upon your death, oh, Hero of Light."
Marrec’s expression remained angry.
He had just failed to protect a key member of the organization, someone whose survival was important to their future plans.
His gaze moved across Luke’s body, and his expression became more serious when he saw that Luke was still standing there without any obvious injury after taking the full force of his aura release.
’Seems like we have to take this seriously.’
If the battle continued here and Luke used that strange chain ability again, Marrec feared that he might be restrained once more, allowing Luke to escape before he could stop him.
"You forced me."
Upon hearing this, Luke’s eyebrows lifted slightly.
The words immediately reminded him of something.
’Villains normally say this dialogue when they’re about to do something out of the scale.’
Unfortunately, he realized it a little too late.
Marrec reached into his belongings and pulled out an ancient scroll.
The scroll looked old enough that its surface had darkened with age, but before Luke could determine what it was, flames suddenly spread across it.
The entire scroll burned almost instantly.
"Hahaha."
Marrec’s laughter returned.
At the same time, the ten Platinum Knights slowly recovered from being blasted into the walls and began moving back toward him.
Once they had regrouped beside him, Marrec looked toward Luke.
"Oh, Hero of Light. Now you will see the real truth of this place."
"Hahahaha!"
His laughter echoed through the ruins.
As he laughed, his transformation began to progress further.
The remaining human portion of his face twisted as the demonic characteristics spread across it, gradually replacing the last traces of his human appearance.
His face became completely demonic.
At the same time, the black horns on his head grew larger.
Once the transformation was complete, Marrec spread both arms wide, his posture resembling someone welcoming an audience into a grand spectacle.
"WELCOME TO THE COLOSSEUM, WHERE YOUR GODS SAW MORTALS FIGHT AND ENJOYED THEIR MISERY!"
His voice grew louder, echoing through the ancient ruins.
Isaria and Kiki immediately moved closer to Luke.
Neither of them knew exactly what was about to happen, but something about Marrec’s words and the ancient surroundings made the situation feel increasingly wrong.
"WELCOME TO THE HEAVEN’S CRUCIBLE!"
The instant Marrec finished speaking, the entire ancient ruin shook.
RUMBLE!
The vibration traveled beneath their feet and through the surrounding walls, growing stronger as the ancient structure began to awaken.
The dark pathways, which had remained motionless for countless years, finally moved again.
Massive sections of the walls began sliding away from their original positions.
At first, the movement was slow.
Then another section shifted.
And another.
The enormous walls began separating from one another, moving farther apart while each section slid into a different position.
It looked almost like a gigantic jigsaw puzzle being taken apart and rearranged piece by piece.
The dark pathways that had once formed a maze-like network were gradually losing their original arrangement as the walls moved into a circular formation.
An arena was taking shape.
"Luke."
Isaria reached out and grabbed his hand.
Her fingers tightened around his as she looked around anxiously, clearly unsettled by the movement taking place around them.
Luke didn’t answer immediately.
His attention remained fixed on the location where Marrec had previously been standing.
It was empty.
Four dark walls had closed around them, separating their section from the rest of the ruins.
Even the ground beneath their feet had changed.
As the structure continued moving, Luke noticed that the ground itself was made from the same dark material as the walls.
The movement also pushed away the dirt and sand that had accumulated over countless years, forcing it toward the edges of the hall where it gathered in thin lines.
Everything was being rearranged.
It was almost as though the ancient ruins themselves were carrying them toward a predetermined position.
"Kiki?"
Kiki nudged Luke’s leg, apparently trying to draw his attention.
However, Luke remained focused on the moving walls.
His eyes traveled across the enormous structure as he calculated the changes taking place around them, trying to understand what the ancient ruins were doing and where exactly they were being taken.
Neither Isaria nor Kiki knew what he was analyzing.
’I have to find Selene.’
Luke kept his expression controlled as he continued observing the transformation.
He couldn’t afford to become worried and rush into action.
If he allowed his concern for Selene to make him act hastily, he could easily overlook something important.
So, for now, he waited.
There was nothing else he could do.
He, Isaria, and Kiki could only remain where they were as the ancient arena continued rearranging itself around them.
The violent shaking gradually began to weaken.
The enormous walls slowed as they approached their final positions, and one by one, the moving sections settled into place.
The vibrations beneath their feet finally diminished.
The ancient ruins slowly became quiet again.
The Heaven’s Crucible had awakened.

Crack!
The shackles around his ankles shattered as well.
"Well, there goes my fifty percent energy."
Seeing this, Luke could only sigh.
It wasn’t that he was disappointed in the seal.
Quite the opposite.
The Seal of Restraint had performed remarkably well, especially considering that Marrec was a mid-B-rank and had been forced to use a special transformation merely to break free.
And there was another advantage.
’I am the Voidheart Titan, meaning I don’t lack either Void or cosmic energy.’
A faint smile appeared on Luke’s face.
With that, his Cosmic Heart immediately began pumping more energy throughout his body, replenishing his reserves at an extremely rapid pace.
After the fusion, he could even generate the energy of his other Titans through the Cosmic Heart.
Like currently, he could also generate void energy.
That had been impossible before.
Unfortunately, the Nexus Titan ability still had a limitation.
It allowed him to use the abilities of his other Titans regardless of the form he was currently using, but it didn’t grant him their inherent characteristics.
In other words, if Luke wanted to directly control Void energy, he still had to transform into the Void Titan.
Otherwise, he could use the abilities he already possessed, but he couldn’t simply gain basic Void elemental control.
’Maybe my Nexus Titan hasn’t fully developed yet.’
Luke considered the possibility.
’Or maybe it’s related to my Titan Knight Origin Skill.’
He was still thinking about it when Marrec’s voice pulled him back to the present.
"You have called upon your death, oh, Hero of Light."
Marrec’s expression remained angry.
He had just failed to protect a key member of the organization, someone whose survival was important to their future plans.
His gaze moved across Luke’s body, and his expression became more serious when he saw that Luke was still standing there without any obvious injury after taking the full force of his aura release.
’Seems like we have to take this seriously.’
If the battle continued here and Luke used that strange chain ability again, Marrec feared that he might be restrained once more, allowing Luke to escape before he could stop him.
"You forced me."
Upon hearing this, Luke’s eyebrows lifted slightly.
The words immediately reminded him of something.
’Villains normally say this dialogue when they’re about to do something out of the scale.’
Unfortunately, he realized it a little too late.
Marrec reached into his belongings and pulled out an ancient scroll.
The scroll looked old enough that its surface had darkened with age, but before Luke could determine what it was, flames suddenly spread across it.
The entire scroll burned almost instantly.
"Hahaha."
Marrec’s laughter returned.
At the same time, the ten Platinum Knights slowly recovered from being blasted into the walls and began moving back toward him.
Once they had regrouped beside him, Marrec looked toward Luke.
"Oh, Hero of Light.
Now you will see the real truth of this place."
"Hahahaha!"
His laughter echoed through the ruins.
As he laughed, his transformation began to progress further.
The remaining human portion of his face twisted as the demonic characteristics spread across it, gradually replacing the last traces of his human appearance.
His face became completely demonic.
At the same time, the black horns on his head grew larger.
Once the transformation was complete, Marrec spread both arms wide, his posture resembling someone welcoming an audience into a grand spectacle.
"WELCOME TO THE COLOSSEUM, WHERE YOUR GODS SAW MORTALS FIGHT AND ENJOYED THEIR MISERY!"
His voice grew louder, echoing through the ancient ruins.
Isaria and Kiki immediately moved closer to Luke.
Neither of them knew exactly what was about to happen, but something about Marrec’s words and the ancient surroundings made the situation feel increasingly wrong.
"WELCOME TO THE HEAVEN’S CRUCIBLE!"
The instant Marrec finished speaking, the entire ancient ruin shook.
RUMBLE!
The vibration traveled beneath their feet and through the surrounding walls, growing stronger as the ancient structure began to awaken.
The dark pathways, which had remained motionless for countless years, finally moved again.
Massive sections of the walls began sliding away from their original positions.
At first, the movement was slow.
Then another section shifted.
And another.
The enormous walls began separating from one another, moving farther apart while each section slid into a different position.
It looked almost like a gigantic jigsaw puzzle being taken apart and rearranged piece by piece.
The dark pathways that had once formed a maze-like network were gradually losing their original arrangement as the walls moved into a circular formation.
An arena was taking shape.
"Luke."
Isaria reached out and grabbed his hand.
Her fingers tightened around his as she looked around anxiously, clearly unsettled by the movement taking place around them.
Luke didn’t answer immediately.
His attention remained fixed on the location where Marrec had previously been standing.
It was empty.
Four dark walls had closed around them, separating their section from the rest of the ruins.
Even the ground beneath their feet had changed.
As the structure continued moving, Luke noticed that the ground itself was made from the same dark material as the walls.
The movement also pushed away the dirt and sand that had accumulated over countless years, forcing it toward the edges of the hall where it gathered in thin lines.
Everything was being rearranged.
It was almost as though the ancient ruins themselves were carrying them toward a predetermined position.
"Kiki?"
Kiki nudged Luke’s leg, apparently trying to draw his attention.
However, Luke remained focused on the moving walls.
His eyes traveled across the enormous structure as he calculated the changes taking place around them, trying to understand what the ancient ruins were doing and where exactly they were being taken.
Neither Isaria nor Kiki knew what he was analyzing.
’I have to find Selene.’
Luke kept his expression controlled as he continued observing the transformation.
He couldn’t afford to become worried and rush into action.
If he allowed his concern for Selene to make him act hastily, he could easily overlook something important.
So, for now, he waited.
There was nothing else he could do.
He, Isaria, and Kiki could only remain where they were as the ancient arena continued rearranging itself around them.
The violent shaking gradually began to weaken.
The enormous walls slowed as they approached their final positions, and one by one, the moving sections settled into place.
The vibrations beneath their feet finally diminished.
The ancient ruins slowly became quiet again.
The Heaven’s Crucible had awakened.

chapters.title: Chapter 300: Fate Has Led Luke Into an Impossible Trap!
paragraphs: Sorry for the inconvenience, and thank you for your understanding.
Luke had already returned to his normal form when his body collided with the dark wall.
Then, finally, the vibrations stopped.
Luke, Isaria, and Kiki slowly looked straight ahead.
The dark walls that had previously surrounded them from every direction had disappeared.
Instead, an enormous empty space had appeared before them.
The dark walls were still present, but they now stood roughly a hundred kilo meters away, forming a circular boundary around a massive arena.
The arena itself stretched for nearly one hundred kilometers in diameter.
Countless spectator seats had also appeared around the battlefield, rising in circles.
Yet not a single person occupied them.
Luke and the others were standing on one side of the arena, attached to a strange structure that resembled another set of elevated spectator seats.
And they weren’t alone.
The others who had entered the ruins had also appeared there.
Selene, Estelle.
The members of the Horizon Astralis Academy.
Even the black-robed man and the people standing beside him.
Luke’s gaze, however, didn’t remain on any of them.
Instead, it moved toward the opposite end of the structure.
An ancient gate stood there.
Luke’s eyes widened.
’What the fuck?!’
It was the exact same ancient gate he had encountered during his first Origin Fragment quest.
At that time...
The System had also appeared.
[Fate has played you again.]
Before Luke could even ask what those words meant, another screen appeared before him.
[SSS+ Rank Chain Quest Triggered!]
[SECOND ORIGIN FRAGMENT]
Description:
Rather than you finding the Origin Fragment...
The Origin Fragment has found you.
Fate has once again played its role.
A coincidence?
Or was it merely another piece moving according to a plan that had already begun long before you arrived?
No one can say.
But there is one thing even Fate may have failed to understand.
Even Fate can make mistakes.
When even forgotten existences, stronger than Gods, could not escape their conspiracy...
When even those ancient beings, whose names have already disappeared from the memories of countless worlds, were trapped within their calculations...
Then how dare Fate believe it could make a perfect calculation?
Those beings have already woven their web far deeper than she can imagine.
Every possibility and variable.
Even the beings that should never have been discovered...
They were already within their calculations.
And now...
You have unknowingly stepped into that same web.
[QUEST OBJECTIVE]
[PATH I — ESCAPE THE ANOMALY]
Do not confront what lies beyond the Origin Fragment.
Do not attempt to uncover what they have hidden.
Because the moment you escape...
The consequences will not end with you.
Selene, Estelle, and Isaria will be destroyed.
Even the Eldric Sunborn Kingdom will be destroyed.
And you will lose one of your most precious parts.
That will only be the beginning.
From that moment onward...
The countdown toward the doom of you and your wives will begin.
You may survive today.
But you will lose everything tomorrow.
[PATH II — FACE THE ANOMALY]
Enter the place where the Second Origin Fragment awaits.
Uncover what lies beyond the ancient gate.
Discover why the Origin Fragment has found you instead of the other way around.
However...
Be prepared to die.
Because this Origin Fragment... is not what you think it is.
The existence behind it is not what you expected.
The truth hidden within it is not something that should have been discovered this easily.
And the conspiracy behind it... has already succeeded.
Their web was created long before you arrived.
You were not the only one who discovered their scheme.
You merely stepped into a position they had already prepared.
Even worse...
Fate itself unknowingly assisted them.
What you believed to be Fate guiding you toward the Origin Fragment... may have been nothing more than Fate helping their plan move forward.
[WARNING]
The first Origin Fragment was a trial.
The second Origin Fragment is different.
[QUEST REWARD]
Rather than receiving a single-rank evolution...
Your Origin Skill will evolve by TWO ranks.
[FINAL SYSTEM NOTICE]
Fate may have brought you here.
But Fate does not understand what is waiting beyond that gate.
Those beings do.
And that is what makes this situation dangerous.
Quest Difficulty: Peak B Rank.
Luke stared at the quest for several seconds.
His expression gradually became more serious.
This quest was clearly telling him that what waited beyond that gate would not be simple.
Far too many uncertainties had already appeared.
’Uncertainties?’
That thought immediately reminded Luke of those hidden beings.
The beings that had trapped the Origin Titan.
The beings that had even corrupted his fragments.
Before he could think any further—
"Luke!"
Selene’s voice suddenly rang out.
Luke turned his head.
Selene was already moving toward him.
She crossed the distance between them and hugged him tightly.
Her body trembled slightly as she held onto him.
"You are safe..."
The relief in her whispered voice was obvious.
Luke’s expression softened.
He gently placed a hand against her back.
And the tension that had been visible in his expression moments ago had eased slightly.
Nearby, Isaria clenched her fist quietly.
Yet, she didn’t say anything.
On the opposite side, Marius gritted his teeth.
His gaze remained fixed on Luke and Selene.
The sight clearly irritated him.
Luke ignored him.
For the moment, he chose to put the strange quest aside.
There was something far more immediate to deal with.
His gaze shifted toward the opposing group.
"Infernal Choir..."
Zeyr and several others also followed his gaze.
The black-robed group stood there without any apparent concern.
Instead, they looked strangely calm, as though they had already expected this situation.
Then everyone’s attention shifted toward the fifty B-Rank warriors standing beside them.
Several expressions immediately changed.
Fifty B-Rank members of the Sunborn Kingdom.
Traitors.
Estelle’s face became especially cold.
She had never expected so many traitors to have been hiding among them.
Several other Sunborn warriors also stared at the group in disbelief.
Before anyone could say anything—
BOOOOOOM!
A thunderous sound echoed through the entire ruins.
The enormous arena trembled.
Then a gigantic blue figure suddenly appeared near them.
The being was nearly one hundred meters tall.
A blue spirit.
"Welcome..."
His thunderous voice spread throughout the entire arena.
"...to Heaven’s Crucible!"
The sudden appearance startled almost everyone.
Even the more experienced representatives couldn’t hide their surprise.
Only the Infernal Choir remained calm.
The blue spirit looked around the arena with a faint smile.
"It’s been a long time since so many people have gathered for this arena."
His gaze swept across the participants.
Then it stopped.
"Hmm?"
His expression changed slightly.
"A Champion Representative."
Several people immediately looked toward the black-robed group in confusion.
The blue spirit didn’t explain.
Instead, he calmly continued.
"Since you are a representative of Iveron, I will allow one High B-Rank participant and two Mid B-Rank participants to present."
Upon hearing this, everyone’s pupils contracted.
Because, only an Early B-Rank should have been able to enter these ruins.
Yet this spirit was openly allowing the enemy stronger beings present.
A High B-Rank.
Two Mid B-Ranks.
And they were clearly on the opposing side.
Several people exchanged uneasy glances.
Then someone noticed something else.
Ivar was missing.
The realization spread quickly.
Some began wondering whether the Infernal Choir had already killed him.
Meanwhile, the leader of the Infernal Choir simply bowed towards the blue spirit.
"Thank you."
The blue spirit merely waved his hand.
He didn’t appear particularly interested in their gratitude.
Instead, he looked toward everyone.
"Since Heaven’s Crucible has already been activated..."
His voice echoed across the arena.
"...then let us finish this competition as well."
He smiled.
"You may choose your own teams."
Several people immediately began looking toward their allies.
The blue spirit continued.
"There will be three rounds."
"Each round will test something different."
His gaze slowly swept across the two sides.
"Once all three rounds are completed, a victorious team will be decided."
Then he raised one hand.
[ ROUND ONE ]
THOUSAND BEASTS
Type: Survival Trial
"One thousand Early B-Rank beasts will be released throughout the arena."
A low murmur immediately spread among the participants.
One thousand Early B-Rank beasts.
Even for the strongest people present, that was not an insignificant number.
"The two teams must fight the beasts and survive until the trial ends."
"The beasts will attack both teams indiscriminately."
"All beasts will be Early B-Rank."
"You may cooperate freely with your teammates."
"Leaving the designated battlefield is prohibited."
"Every beast you defeat will contribute toward your team’s score."
"The round will end once the required survival period has been completed."
The blue spirit paused.
"The team that defeats the greater number of beasts will win the round."
Several people exchanged serious looks.
[ ROUND TWO ]
WAR OF FLAGS
Type: Territory / Strategic Trial
"Several divine banners will be scattered throughout the battlefield."
"These banners cannot be destroyed by ordinary attacks."
"Capture them."
"Hold them."
"Protect them."
"Or take them from your enemy."
His voice remained calm.
"A team gains points for every banner under its control."
"The longer a banner remains under your control, the more points you will receive."
"Any team member may capture a banner."
"Captured banners can be stolen."
"Combat between participants is permitted."
"The round will end when the designated time expires."
He looked at everyone.
"The team with the highest number of points will win."
The atmosphere became slightly more tense.
[ ROUND THREE ]
WAR OF THE CHOSEN
Type: Individual Death Match
"This is the final round."
"Every participant will receive the blessing of Heaven’s Crucible."
A faint blue light began spreading throughout the arena.
"This blessing will allow every participant to fight at the absolute limit of their current realm."
Several people immediately focused their attention.
"After receiving the blessing, both teams will select their warriors."
"One warrior from each side will enter the battlefield."
"The two warriors will fight."
"The winner remains."
"The defeated warrior is removed from the current match."
Several people exchanged glances at that rule.
Then the blue spirit continued.
"The winning warrior will be completely restored before the next battle."
That caused several expressions to change.
A powerful warrior wouldn’t simply be worn down through repeated battles.
They could recover after every victory.
"The winning warrior may continue fighting as long as they remain undefeated."
"Either side may surrender before receiving a lethal blow."
"Once a participant surrenders, they are considered defeated."
His voice then became colder.
"However..."
"Death is permitted only for third round."
"As for first and second round."
"If a warrior dies, then their body will transform into light."
"They will then be revived at their team’s camp."
After that, The blue spirit immediately continued.
"The battle will continue until one team has no undefeated warrior remaining."
The blue spirit raised his hand again.
"That is not all."
[ VICTORY BONUS ]
"Every time a warrior defeats an opposing participant, five enhancement choices will appear."
"The warrior may choose one."
"The selected enhancement will remain active for the remainder of the round."
"And every new victory..."
His smile widened slightly.
"...will provide another selection."
The meaning was immediately understood.
A warrior who continued winning would gradually become stronger.
The participants would need to decide carefully who they sent into each battle.
"Finally..."
The blue spirit spread his arms.
"Each completed round will provide rewards."
"Round One will reward the team according to its survival and number of defeated beasts."
"Round Two will reward the team according to its accumulated points and captured banners."
"And Round Three..."
He paused.
"...will determine the ultimate victor."
"The victorious team will receive the greatest reward."
The blue spirit slowly lowered his hands.
"These are the rules of Heaven’s Crucible."
"Form your teams."
"Prepare yourselves."
A faint smile appeared on his face.
"Once the first round begins..."
His gaze passed across everyone present.
"...Heaven’s Crucible will not care who you are."
"Only whether you can survive."
